item.title: The New York Knicks championship player who will not be attending tonight’s ring ceremony
item.description: Photo by Sarah Stier/Getty Images The New York Knicks are set to hold their Banner Night on October 20, which will include their 2026 championship-winning team collecting their rings. The Knicks clash with the Philadelphia 76ers to kick off their first season as defending champions in over five decades. Key names like Josh Hart, Jalen Brunson and center Karl-Anthony Towns are expected to feature in the game and also collect their rings at the ceremony. Several now-former Knicks stars should also be in attendance to collect their prizes, with Mitchell Robinson the only one not able to do so. Mitchell Robinson won’t be available for New York Knicks ring ceremony Robinson joined the Knicks back in 2018 and played an important role in their NBA Finals win over the San Antonio Spurs. However, he has now departed, signing a three-year, $47.4 million contract with the Boston Celtics in July. The Celtics are playing the Detroit Pistons on October 20, so Mitchell will have to wait until March 2027, when the Knicks host the Celtics, to collect his ring. Elsewhere, there are four more former Knicks players who were part of the side in 2025/26 who should be in attendance on Tuesday to get their rings, even though they no longer play for the team. Dillon Jones joined the 76ers after departing the Knicks earlier this year but he was waived on October 17. The Portland Trail Blazers confirmed this past weekend that they had waived Jeremy Sochan. Meanwhile, Trey Jemison III was officially waived by the Toronto Raptors on October 14. Finally, Ariel Hukporti joined the 76ers over the summer so he was going to be at the season opener anyway. But he will play no part in the on-court action, as he has ruptured his Achilles tendon and will miss the entire 2026/27 NBA season. As a result, every player barring Robinson should be collecting their championship rings on Tuesday. item.title: Is LeBron James playing tonight? Sixers projected starting lineup vs. Knicks
item.description: The King James era in Philly is finally here. NBA legend LeBron James will finally make his Philadelphia 76ers debut tonight as the Sixers tipoff off the 2026-2027 season against the reigning champion New York Knicks . Along with James, former Boston Celtics star Jaylen Brown also is set to appear in a Sixers jersey for the first time following a shocked offseason trade that sent Paul George and picks to the Celtics. The two All-NBA forwards will be joined by Sixers stars Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey and V.J. Edgecombe as Philly looks to ruin the NBA-title banner night for Jalen Brunson, Karl-Anthony Towns and the rest of the Knicks and their fans. Here's the projected starting lineups. Is LeBron James playing tonight? James is set to make his regular season NBA debut with the 76ers tonight against the Knicks. Sixers projected starting lineup with LeBron James With James signing with Philadelphia, the Sixers would potentially have one of the most talented starting lineups in the NBA. Here's what it might look it: Sixers potential starting lineup Joel Embiid, C LeBron James, PF Jaylon Brown, SF V.J. Edgecombe, G Tyrese Maxey, G Knicks projected starting lineup Knicks potential starting lineup Karl-Anthony Towns, C OG Anunoby, F Mikal Bridges, F Josh Hart, G Jalen Brunson, G 76ers injury report Dean Wade: Questionable (ankle) Adem Bona: Questionable (foot) Anfernee Simons: Questionable (hamstring) Tacko Fall: Out (hip) Dominick Barlow: Out (Likely to miss two weeks with lumbar spine bone stress response) Knicks injury report No injuries to report What time is Sixers game tonight? The Sixers-Knicks season opener will tipoff at 7 p.m. ET. What channel is the Sixers game tonight? The Sixers-Knicks season opener will be broadcast on nationally. Here's how to watch: TV: NBC Streaming: Peacock LeBron James helicopter commute with sixers Fortunately for James, it will be a short commute and he won't have to his a helicopter to commute to the game since it will be in New York. As part of a deal with former 76ers and current Fanatics owner Michael Rubin, James has unlimited access to use a helicopter to take flights back and forth from NYC to games in Philly. What jersey number will LeBron James wear with the Sixers? The Sixers made it official on July 27 that James will wear No. 23. LeBron James Sixers jersey LeBron James jerseys are now available via the NBA's official retailer, Fanatics . They are for preorder only and will ship on or before Aug. 21. item.description: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - SEPTEMBER 12: Jonathan Taylor #28 of the Indianapolis Colts runs the ball in the game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lucas Oil Stadium on September 12, 2021 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images There’s a flurry of issues on offense for our beloved Seattle Seahawks. Struggling and reeling a bit, the team is most likely looking for answers. With the possibility of a mid-season trade, is there something to the fact that a better running back makes this a functioning offense all of a sudden? Or, is the work too varied for there to be one solution to a larger problem? The Seahawks have work to do. Trying something is inevitable. Would you make a trade happen? item.title: Here's Why the Celtics Are Playing at 3 PM Today
item.description: Here's Why the Celtics Are Playing at 3 PM Today originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Your eyes haven't deceived you. The Boston Celtics are playing at 3 p.m. today. The Celtics will face the Detroit Pistons to kick off the 2026-27 NBA season. While it's not a surprise to see them as one of the teams playing on Opening Day, the early start certainly is unusual. Here's why the NBA and NBC decided to shake things up. MORE: Joe Mazzulla Sets Bold Goal That Could Define Celtics' Season Why Celtics Are Playing at 3 p.m. Today Shortly after news broke that the Celtics would open the season with an afternoon game, ESPN's Dave McMenamin shared why the NBA made the decision. "I've talked to people around the league today, and they're like, we could sense the excitement for the NBA right now, so let's experiment with this thing," said McMenamin . "They talked with executives at NBC, and it was kind of a joint decision that this is something we can turn into a celebration of the game. It's already a marquee moment for the league. Let's see if we can enhance it and turn it into a major showcase. "Maybe down the line, this becomes a tradition for NBA fans. It's not that abnormal to see sporting events during the daytime in America. Also, an added bonus: it's an international game. 3 p.m. Eastern is prime time viewing in Europe." Pistons head coach J.B. Bickerstaff said Monday that the early start "is what it is." He added that he understands the benefit of making it a friendlier time for international markets and praised the league for finding ways to grow its fanbase. It's a particularly convenient time for England, where the game will tip at 8 p.m., and much of continental Europe, where it'll begin at 9 p.m. It'll be interesting to see if this is a one-off or the start of a new tradition. item.title: NBA power rankings: All 30 teams ranked entering 2026-27 season
item.description: The 2026-27 NBA season begins this week. The past few seasons have shown just how much parity exists across the NBA, and this season has the potential to be the wildest yet. After a preseason filled with new faces in new places, here are the first NBA power rankings of the season. MORE: Ranking top 7 NBA rookies entering 2026-27 season Ranks 30-25 Oct 7, 2026; Memphis, Tennessee, USA; Memphis Grizzlies forward Cameron Boozer (27) looks on during the second quarter against the Orlando Magic at FedExForum. Mandatory Credit: Petre Thomas-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) 30. Memphis Grizzlies Memphis remains at the bottom of the league despite finishing the preseason 3-1. Cedric Coward and Cameron Boozer headline a young roster with potential, but the Grizzlies still lack the talent and experience needed to compete with the league’s best teams. Their preseason success is encouraging, but there is still plenty of work to do. 29. Los Angeles Clippers The Clippers added guard Keaton Wagler with the fifth overall pick in the draft, giving them a young player to build around. Los Angeles finished the preseason 2-1, but a few exhibition wins won’t solve the franchise’s larger problems. The penalties stemming from the Kawhi Leonard scandal have created additional obstacles, leaving the Clippers with a difficult road ahead. 28. Sacramento Kings Sacramento enters the season with plenty of questions after finishing the preseason 0-5. Darius Acuff has been inconsistent during his first preseason appearances, but he has shown flashes of an explosive scoring guard. Veterans Zach LaVine and Domantas Sabonis should keep the Kings competitive on certain nights, but the roster still has significant weaknesses that could make for a long season. 27. Milwaukee Bucks Milwaukee finished the preseason 2-3, offering a mixed outlook after the end of the Giannis Antetokounmpo era. The Bucks face a difficult transition without their former franchise centerpiece, and the roster has yet to establish a clear identity. Milwaukee has some pieces to build around, but it will likely struggle to compete with the Eastern Conference’s top teams. 26. Brooklyn Nets Brooklyn has an interesting mix of veterans and young talent. Michael Porter Jr. and Julius Randle headline the veteran group, while lottery pick Mikel Brown Jr. and Egor Demin could form an exciting young backcourt. The Nets finished the preseason 3-1, providing some early encouragement. Although a playoff push remains unlikely, Brooklyn has reasons to be optimistic about its future. 25. Dallas Mavericks Dallas finished the preseason 1-3, but the results shouldn’t be a major concern. Kyrie Irving returns from injury, while rookie Morez Johnson adds another young piece to the roster. With Dusty May taking over as head coach, the Mavericks have an opportunity to develop their young talent. They might not be ready to contend, but a surprise run toward the play-in tournament isn’t out of the question

Dallas Mavericks Dallas finished the preseason 1-3, but the results shouldn’t be a major concern. Kyrie Irving returns from injury, while rookie Morez Johnson adds another young piece to the roster. With Dusty May taking over as head coach, the Mavericks have an opportunity to develop their young talent. They might not be ready to contend, but a surprise run toward the play-in tournament isn’t out of the question. Ranks 24-17 Oct 11, 2026; Charlotte, North Carolina, USA; Charlotte Hornets center Naz Reid (0) looks on during warm ups against the Milwaukee Bucks at Spectrum Center. Mandatory Credit: Scott Kinser-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) 24. Charlotte Hornets Charlotte took a step backward this offseason by trading LaMelo Ball after six years with the franchise. Naz Reid arrived in the deal, while Coby White is expected to take over Ball’s role in the backcourt. The Hornets finished the preseason 1-3, and their roster still has plenty of questions. After reaching the play-in picture, Charlotte could find itself back in the lottery. 23. Chicago Bulls Chicago has plenty of reasons to be excited about its future. The Bulls finished the preseason 3-2, with rookie of the year candidate Caleb Wilson leading the way. The franchise also made significant changes to its personnel and front office this offseason. Chicago still has work to do, but a young roster with something to prove could keep the Bulls in the play-in race. 22. Phoenix Suns Phoenix returns much of its roster while adding Miles Bridges and several depth pieces. However, a 1-4 preseason record did little to inspire confidence. The Suns have enough talent to compete for a play-in spot, but they lack the overall depth and star power needed to challenge the Western Conference’s top teams. 21. Utah Jazz Darynn Peterson, the second overall pick in the 2026 draft, joins Keyonte George, Jaren Jackson Jr. and Lauri Markkanen. The Jazz finished the preseason 3-1, showing some early promise as their young players continue to develop. Their lack of experience keeps them outside the playoff conversation for now, but their long-term potential is worth watching. 20. Orlando Magic Orlando is relying on its core of Paolo Banchero, Franz Wagner and Desmond Bane to lead the way. The addition of Nikola Vucevic gives the Magic another option behind Wendell Carter Jr. Orlando finished the preseason 3-1, and with continuity on its side, the team has a chance to take another step forward. 19. Washington Wizards The Wizards added Anthony Davis, extended Trae Young and selected AJ Dybantsa with the first overall pick. Washington finished the preseason 2-2, but their potential extends beyond a handful of exhibition games. If the pieces fit together, the Wizards could emerge as a surprise contender. 18. New Orleans Pelicans The Pelicans finished the preseason 3-1. New Orleans added AJ Johnson and Benedict Mathurin this offseason, giving an already promising roster more scoring options. If Zion Williamson and Dejounte Murray stay healthy, New Orleans could compete for a postseason spot. 17. Atlanta Hawks Atlanta brought in Luguentz Dort, Aaron Wiggins and Kingston Flemings. Dort adds much-needed defensive toughness alongside Dyson Daniels, while Wiggins and Flemings provide additional options. The Hawks finished the preseason 4-1, one of the stronger records in the Eastern Conference. If their offseason additions come together, Atlanta could be a difficult matchup throughout the season. Ranks 16-11 Sep 28, 2026; Indianapolis, IN, USA; Indiana Pacers guard Tyrese Haliburton (0) poses for a photo during media day. Mandatory Credit: Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) 16. Indiana Pacers The Pacers are no longer the same team that reached the NBA Finals two seasons ago. Indiana finished the preseason 1-3, although the results matter less than how quickly Haliburton can regain his rhythm. 15. Golden State Warriors Golden State finished the preseason 4-2, showing some encouraging signs ahead of the regular season. As long as Stephen Curry is on the court, Golden State has a chance to compete. The Warriors added Yaxel Lendeborg in the lottery and will benefit from Jimmy Butler’s return from injury. 14. Portland Trail Blazers Portland enters the season with a new identity following the addition of Ja Morant and Damian Lillard’s return. Deni Avdija’s All-Star-level play gives the Trail Blazers another reliable offensive option. Portland finished the preseason 2-1, but its regular-season ceiling will depend on how quickly its new pieces develop chemistry. 13. Toronto Raptors Toronto brings Kawhi Leonard back to the city where he helped deliver the franchise’s first championship. item.title: From dirt to turf: FIFA’s record investments boost emerging nations
item.description: From dirt to turf: FIFA’s record investments boost emerging nations Through significantly increased funding and greater access to tournaments, developing football markets such as Mauritania, Bangladesh and Bhutan are building sustainable sporting structures for the long term. For many emerging football nations, FIFA represents the main, if not the only, reliable source of income. Recent financial figures and institutional policy changes point to a concerted effort by the governing body to build sustainable structures in these markets, focusing on three pillars: financial support, talent development and greater access to tournaments. The financial progression is clear. Under the FIFA Forward programme, funding for each member association has risen from $3.8 million (2016–2018 cycle) to $8 million in the current 2023–2026 cycle. A new proposal on the table for 2027–2030 aims to give each association a total of $25 million. Ahmed Yahya, president of the Mauritanian Football Federation, highlighted the practical impact of these figures following a recent FIFA Council meeting. "These financial resources allow today's young people to play on grass pitches rather than rocky ground or dirt pitches, and that is precisely what matters," Yahya explained. He stressed the fundamental importance of equal funding and voting rights for all nations. "For us, equality is what defines FIFA today. Gianni Infantino is moving football forward around the world... The majority want him to stay." Crucially, this financial backing is combined with FIFA's Talent Development Scheme and the expansion of youth tournaments. By helping associations identify and nurture talent while providing more platforms on the world stage, FIFA is seeking to create a structure in which football becomes a genuine career option in developing regions. In Bangladesh, this combined strategy is delivering tangible results. Tabith Awal, president of the Bangladesh Football Federation, pointed to recent milestones, including a historic victory over San Marino during a European international window and an invitation to the FIFA ASEAN Cup. "We have made use of many of FIFA's good projects, whether the Arena programme or the Forward programme, to truly develop a football culture in Bangladesh," Awal said. Awal also highlighted the current administration's hands-on approach to governance, noting that Infantino "continues to extend the hand of friendship" even when faced with institutional disagreements. A recent brief stopover by the FIFA president in Dhaka allowed local officials to demonstrate exactly how international funds are being allocated on the ground. This strategy of global visibility extends to Bhutan, which recently welcomed a FIFA president to the country for the first time in its history. The visit underscored a broader administrative goal: maintaining direct contact with all member associations, regardless of their size, and allowed local leaders to map out the future. Dasho Ugen Tsechup

For many emerging football nations, FIFA represents the main, if not the only, reliable source of income. Recent financial figures and institutional policy changes point to a concerted effort by the governing body to build sustainable structures in these markets, focusing on three pillars: financial support, talent development and greater access to tournaments. The financial progression is clear. Under the FIFA Forward programme, funding for each member association has risen from $3.8 million (2016–2018 cycle) to $8 million in the current 2023–2026 cycle. A new proposal on the table for 2027–2030 aims to give each association a total of $25 million. Ahmed Yahya, president of the Mauritanian Football Federation, highlighted the practical impact of these figures following a recent FIFA Council meeting. "These financial resources allow today's young people to play on grass pitches rather than rocky ground or dirt pitches, and that is precisely what matters," Yahya explained. He stressed the fundamental importance of equal funding and voting rights for all nations. "For us, equality is what defines FIFA today. Gianni Infantino is moving football forward around the world... The majority want him to stay." Crucially, this financial backing is combined with FIFA's Talent Development Scheme and the expansion of youth tournaments. By helping associations identify and nurture talent while providing more platforms on the world stage, FIFA is seeking to create a structure in which football becomes a genuine career option in developing regions. In Bangladesh, this combined strategy is delivering tangible results. Tabith Awal, president of the Bangladesh Football Federation, pointed to recent milestones, including a historic victory over San Marino during a European international window and an invitation to the FIFA ASEAN Cup. "We have made use of many of FIFA's good projects, whether the Arena programme or the Forward programme, to truly develop a football culture in Bangladesh," Awal said. Awal also highlighted the current administration's hands-on approach to governance, noting that Infantino "continues to extend the hand of friendship" even when faced with institutional disagreements. A recent brief stopover by the FIFA president in Dhaka allowed local officials to demonstrate exactly how international funds are being allocated on the ground. This strategy of global visibility extends to Bhutan, which recently welcomed a FIFA president to the country for the first time in its history. The visit underscored a broader administrative goal: maintaining direct contact with all member associations, regardless of their size, and allowed local leaders to map out the future. Dasho Ugen Tsechup, president of the Bhutan Football Federation (BFF), used the historic visit to outline ambitious future initiatives. "Because of his busy schedule, time was short. But our discussions were concise and straight to the point," Ugen Tsechup explained. "With FIFA's help, much more can now be done in Bhutan." He then detailed a comprehensive development plan that includes the Rama academy and school project for males and females, commercial upgrades to the existing football infrastructure in Changjiji and GMC, and the construction of a new stadium in Paro. When asked to single out one project from the Infantino era that he was most proud of, Ugen Tsechup declined, emphasising the cumulative effect of consistent support. "I cannot single out any one project, because every investment has been an important contribution to the development of football in Bhutan," he said. "The headquarters, which has given us independence... the academy, the infrastructure, the pitches, the mini-pitches, the futsal courts; every single aspect of infrastructure development provided by FIFA has marked an important milestone for our federation." This local investment is having a profound human impact, particularly in women's football. Pema Choden Tshering, captain of the Bhutan women's national team, has witnessed the transformation of grassroots football first-hand. "I grew up playing on dusty pitches. Now I have the opportunity to play on artificial turf and grass pitches through my experiences in international matches," Tshering noted. She pointed to the establishment of a girls' academy in Gelephu—where more than 60 girls receive regular training throughout the year—as a direct result of improved infrastructure. Tshering also credited the FIFA Forward programme with funding valuable match experience that allows the team to test itself internationally. "That has provided many opportunities for the girls to grow, not just as players, but also as people," she added. With national team players now securing international contracts, Tshering is optimistic: "I hope this will also inspire future generations of girls and encourage parents to allow more girls to take up the sport." While elite European football traditionally dominates media coverage, the administrative reality for countries such as Mauritania, Bangladesh and Bhutan is that consistent, structured investment is creating a new foundation. By combining reliable funding with clear talent pathways and grassroots infrastructure, FIFA is laying the groundwork needed for the world's most popular sport to grow equitably across the globe. The Green Bay box score for the game — and I have to use the Phoenix’s website because Marquette has actually deleted the listing from their schedule page — says there was 3,122 people in attendance. That’s in a building that has a Wikipedia-listed capacity of 9,729 for basketball, but 7,500 for end-stage concerts, and I mention that part because the end of the arena on the Green Bay bench end was in fact curtained off completely. Let’s call it half-full at best, and keep that thought in mind relative to the idea that it’s “good for the state” for Marquette to play Green Bay in a regular season game at Fiserv Forum. Was it an exhibition game? Yes. Green Bay also hosted Wisconsin back on October 15th and only drew 4,651 people. I rest my case, your honor. Stat Leaders! Marquette Points: Nigel James, 18 Rebounds: Josh Clark, 6 Assists: Nigel James, 10 Blocks: Sananda Fru, 2 Steals: Nolan Minessale, 3 Minutes: Nigel James, 31 Green Bay Points: Ahmere Carson, 29 Rebounds: Clarence Payia, 4 Assists: LeBron Thomas, 3 Blocks: Clarence Payia & Maruan Cicic, 1 Steals: Marcus Hall, Tadej Colnaric, & Ahmere Carson, 2 Four Factors Marquette Effective Field Goal Percentage: 73.5% Turnover Rate: 22.4% Offensive Rebounding Rate: 36.0% Free Throw Rate: 49.0.% Green Bay Effective Field Goal Percentage: 46.9% Turnover Rate: 20.9% Offensive Rebounding Rate: 12.1% Free Throw Rate: 38.8% How about the 7 minute postgame press availability from Marquette head coach Shaka Smart? Let’s address the Ahmere Carson of it all. Carson finished with 29 points, but he had 27 in the first half thanks to 10-for-10 shooting, which included five three-pointers. That means he went 1-for-4 from the field in the second half, missing his only three-point attempt of the final 20 minutes. If you watch Smart’s press availability, their concern with him going into the game was the ability get out in transition against them, and then he blew up shooting it instead. It sounds like the solution was to just start throwing different looks at Carson to make him uncomfortable, and it clearly worked. I enjoy a nice halftime adjustment, especially on a micro level like that. This also means that the first half score was Marquette 43, Ahmere Carson 27, and Green Bay 11. Carson had eight of his 27 in the first five minutes of the game as Green Bay struck out to what would be their largest lead of the game, 10-4, with 17:38 left in the half. Marquette tied the game at 16 on an Adrien Stevens free throw with 13:35 left before intermission, then Stevens hit his second for a 17-16 lead, and MU would never trail again. The lead shift came in the middle of an 11-0 run by Marquette, and from the moment they tied it to the end of the game, MU outscored the Phoenix 71-44. From the moment of the tie forward, Marquette won the rest of the first half 27-22 while Carson had 19 of his 27 in the first half. 27-3 against the rest of the team, though. It’s worth noting that Marquette was up 35-20 with 7:56 left after two Stevens freebies, a 31-10 run since GB’s largest lead. Yes, Green Bay went on an 18-8 run to the end of the half from there, but 17 of it was Carson. At the end of the day, Marquette was presented with an unexpected challenge, pushed through it to hold an advantage anyway, and then when given a moment to discuss the challenge as a group, came up with a solution and fixed it for the rest of the game. Giving up 27 to one guy in 20 minutes isn’t a fun thing to do, but from a big picture perspective, I think they handled it well. Random thoughts and ideas I had: Damarius Owens swapped with Nolan Minessale in the starting lineup after what we saw in the first two games in the Canada trip. Can’t really count the third one since Adrien Stevens missed that one with an illness. In the post-game, Shaka Smart said that Owens has been the player showing the biggest step forward in preseason practices, so the starting gig here was a reward for that. Owens has been challenged to play defense at a particular level in order to keep that job, so I’m not going to be too concerned with his line of two points, a rebound, and a steal in 18 minutes here, at least not yet. Sananda Fru looks like the real deal. Six points, four rebounds, a steal and two blocks in 23 foul-hampered minutes isn’t jump off the page stuff, but he moves incredibly well and is noticeably vocal on the court, particularly on the defensive end to communicate switches and screens and the like. When Nigel James can do stuff like 18 & 10 with four rebounds, two steals, and a block and it feels like he was quiet, Fru’s not going to be asked to carry a load that shows up on the stat sheet. Thus, it’s going to be the other stuff that makes him valuable to Marquette this season. And so, we should probably turn around right away and discuss his compatriot, Josh Clark. 20 minutes played, perhaps more because of foul trouble for both Fru and Royce Parham, six points, a team high six rebounds, two steals and a block. Do not get over your skis on this quite yet, as Green Bay had one guy with size to go against the 7’1” Clark, but the redshirt sophomore looked like he knew what he wanted to do/what he was supposed to do on a regular basis. That itself is a jump forward for him, and being aware of things at a better level is going to allow him to use his size and strength to a bigger advantage. Also: Smart spent at least two stretches of the game playing Fru and Clark together! I’m curious if that’s more about Parham’s foul troubles in this game, just a lineup laboratory thing in an exhibition game, or something that the Golden Eagles want to actually deploy regularly this year. I’ve brought up Royce Parham’s foul troubles in this game, and that’s putting it lightly. He picked up his second with 7:31 left in the first half, and Shaka Smart actually made him play through it for a while because his first had come at the 18:40 mark and Parham got pulled for a little while after that one. His third and fourth fouls are arguably worse situations. I was sure he was getting thrown out of the game for foul #3, as the in-arena replay made it clear that Parham had yanked a GB screener by the neck as he went around him to contest a corner three, but the refs left it at only a flagrant 1. His fourth foul came with 6:37 left and was the world’s most obvious hook & spin offensive foul that you’ve ever seen. I had a great view of it as he went baseline, and my reaction was “careful, Royce, that’s a whistle more often th—oh, there’s the whistle.” Like I said, very obvious. He finished with 14 points, four rebounds, and two assists in just 17 minutes, so the box score makes him look pretty great in limited minutes, but his decision making was all over the place here. Colin Porter played nine minutes here, the least total minutes out of anyone who appeared in the first half. That’s not terribly surprising given his August addition to the roster, as he’s only had a short amount of time to acclimate to what the coaching staff is going to ask him to do and get used to his teammates. He attempted two three-pointers and made one of them, grabbed two rebounds, dished two assists, and committed a foul that he regretted while he was in the air leaping towards the player he fouled. You could actually see Porter realize “crap, I fouled him” before the contact was made. Do not take anything important away from Porter’s availability here. There’s an active temporary injunction in his lawsuit against the NCAA for a fifth year of eligibility, so he was eligible for this game after not being eligible for the open scrimmage at the beginning of the

item.title: Mike McCarthy Defends Late-Game Play-Calling vs. Bucs: ‘Those Are Solid Plays’
item.description: Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy looks on during the third quarter against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium on Oct 18, 2026; Tampa, Florida. -- Kim Klement Neitzel / Imagn Images IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect PITTSBURGH — Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy doubled down on defending his play calls from the 2-yard line after the Jamel Dean interception late in the fourth quarter against Tampa. “I get the post evaluation, but those are solid plays,” McCarthy said on Monday . Two of the three plays the Steelers ran from the goal line were passes, and when Aaron Rodgers ’ third-down toss to DK Metcalf fell incomplete, the Buccaneers had a timeout remaining and 1:21 to play — just enough time for Jalon Daniels to lead the Bucs into field goal range, which he did. “Absolutely. You’re talking clock. The first down, it was a boot. Then the second down, the run, we caught them with 10 on the field, so you know, it was a substitution and all of those things, but definitely was aware of the clock there,” McCarthy said after the game. Rodgers shared his head coach’s sentiments about the sequence. “The first play wasn’t executed very well, but I think we still had a chance to make the catch. On second down, they were late rotating over, and we just missed the double-team block on the front side. If we get that, it’s probably a walk-in touchdown,” Rodgers explained. “On third down, it was a run-pass option, and I felt like DK [Metcalf] was rolling open. I just missed the throw inside. If I put the ball in a better spot, he catches it and we’re not even having this conversation. Instead, we kicked the field goal. Then they got the ball, put a couple things together, and we had to go make it work in overtime. But I’m proud of the way our guys responded. Obviously, we’d have preferred to put that game away in regulation. Still, these are the kinds of moments that matter most for a team that’s trying to grow. This was a trajectory-altering win. If you fall to 3-3 with a trip to Paris coming up, that’s not where you want to be. Cleveland won today too, so now several teams in the division are sitting at 4-2. That’s why this one was so important. Our guys responded when they had to, and they found a way to get it done.” McCarthy also let precious seconds tick away before calling a timeout after Tampa’s last third-down pass. McCarthy revealed in his postgame press conference that he intended to call a timeout right away after the final Buccaneers play of regulation, but there was a miscommunication between him and the official that let time off the clock. “There’s some miscommunication there. We were thinking right away there at 34, 35 [seconds]. There’s just miscommunication between the ref and I. That’s why it went down as low as it did. But ultimately it worked out,” McCarthy said. McCarthy received a lot of heat for his late-game clock management and play-calling, but the veteran head coach believes he called the right pla

You’re talking clock. The first down, it was a boot. Then the second down, the run, we caught them with 10 on the field, so you know, it was a substitution and all of those things, but definitely was aware of the clock there,” McCarthy said after the game. Rodgers shared his head coach’s sentiments about the sequence. “The first play wasn’t executed very well, but I think we still had a chance to make the catch. On second down, they were late rotating over, and we just missed the double-team block on the front side. If we get that, it’s probably a walk-in touchdown,” Rodgers explained. “On third down, it was a run-pass option, and I felt like DK [Metcalf] was rolling open. I just missed the throw inside. If I put the ball in a better spot, he catches it and we’re not even having this conversation. Instead, we kicked the field goal. Then they got the ball, put a couple things together, and we had to go make it work in overtime. But I’m proud of the way our guys responded. Obviously, we’d have preferred to put that game away in regulation. Still, these are the kinds of moments that matter most for a team that’s trying to grow. This was a trajectory-altering win. If you fall to 3-3 with a trip to Paris coming up, that’s not where you want to be. Cleveland won today too, so now several teams in the division are sitting at 4-2. That’s why this one was so important. Our guys responded when they had to, and they found a way to get it done.” McCarthy also let precious seconds tick away before calling a timeout after Tampa’s last third-down pass. McCarthy revealed in his postgame press conference that he intended to call a timeout right away after the final Buccaneers play of regulation, but there was a miscommunication between him and the official that let time off the clock. “There’s some miscommunication there. We were thinking right away there at 34, 35 [seconds]. There’s just miscommunication between the ref and I. That’s why it went down as low as it did. But ultimately it worked out,” McCarthy said. McCarthy received a lot of heat for his late-game clock management and play-calling, but the veteran head coach believes he called the right plays during the goal-line situation late in the fourth quarter. Alan Saunders provided reporting from Pittsburgh. item.title: 'You've got to dream' - Oxford City draw Leicester
item.description: Oxford City will play Leicester City in the first round proper of the FA Cup [Getty Images] Oxford City chief executive Justin Merritt says his side have "got to dream" after drawing Leicester City in the first round proper of the FA Cup. The sixth-tier Hoops will host the fallen former Premier League champions and 2020-21 FA Cup winners at the MGroup Stadium on the weekend of 6-9 November following Monday night's draw. It is the first time since 2008 that Leicester have taken part at this stage of the competition, with National League North side Oxford City hoping to cause a famous upset. "You've got to dream and be positive," Merritt told BBC Radio Oxford. "For us it's a free shot as they're expected to go through but look at (upsets) in recent years. "It does happen and every round there is a shock or two so why not us?" Leicester have endured a slow start to their League One campaign, with three wins from their first nine games following back-to-back relegations. The Hoops, meanwhile, currently sit third in the National League North table after a fine start to the campaign, winning seven of their 11 matches so far. "Getting a big side like that down here is going to be a terrific occasion," Merritt said. "Not just for the players but also for the fans and the staff that work here day in, day out. "We're really looking forward to it and we really hope the TV people will look at the game as an attractive tie as that will add extra revenue plus the exposure will be absolutely brilliant. "Leicester have experienced a difference in level but not quite coming to play in a tight ground like ours and playing on a 3G surface." Leicester to visit Oxford City in FA Cup first round

item.title: Five takeaways from UConn women’s basketball’s win over Texas
item.description: HARTFORD, CT. — Matchups between two powerhouse programs rarely happen this early, let alone in an exhibition. But when UConn stepped on the floor at PeoplesBank Arena on Monday night, the Huskies made the most of their opportunity as they defeated Texas , 83-61. Star forward Sarah Strong scored a game-high 27 points, and the Huskies did it without Blanca Quiñonez (shoulder), Marine Dursus (foot) and Morgan Cheli (undisclosed injury). For coach Geno Auriemma, the real value was the look at a March-caliber opponent. “I’m glad it’s not March,” Auriemma said. “You don’t want to be playing a game when you’re not quite sure what you have. But March is going to come, and your goal is to play a team like Texas in March because that means you’re going pretty far in the tournament. ... Getting a taste of that, getting a preview of that, is way better than watching on film and talking about it at practice.” Here are the biggest takeaways from Monday’s win: UConn vs Texas highlights: UConn vs Texas exhibition | Huskies surge in second half to down Longhorns UConn vs Syracuse takeaways: Seven observations from UConn women’s basketball’s win over Syracuse Why freshman Olivia Vukosa is ready: Geno Auriemma’s tough talk is a good sign for UConn’s Olivia Vukosa Popovic is outstanding again After a solid showing in her first exhibition game, Jovana Popovic once again showed that she isn’t your average freshman. The Serbian point guard played 36 minutes and scored 22 points on 7-of-11 shooting while grabbing seven rebounds and dishing out five assists. She hit all three of her shots from beyond the arc, hit 5-of-6 of her free throws and registered a plus-minus rating of +25. “The shots she makes are just shots you need when we really need her to make them,” Auriemma said. “She's calm and she's good.” How did the Huskies guard Booker? item.content:encoded: HARTFORD, CT. — Matchups between two powerhouse programs rarely happen this early, let alone in an exhibition. But when UConn stepped on the floor at PeoplesBank Arena on Monday night, the Huskies made the most of their opportunity as they defeated Texas , 83-61. Star forward Sarah Strong scored a game-high 27 points, and the Huskies did it without Blanca Quiñonez (shoulder), Marine Dursus (foot) and Morgan Cheli (undisclosed injury). For coach Geno Auriemma, the real value was the look at a March-caliber opponent. “I’m glad it’s not March,” Auriemma said. “You don’t want to be playing a game when you’re not quite sure what you have. But March is going to come, and your goal is to play a team like Texas in March because that means you’re going pretty far in the tournament. ... Getting a taste of that, getting a preview of that, is way better than watching on film and talking about it at practice.” Here are the biggest takeaways from Monday’s win: UConn vs Texas highlights: UConn vs Texas exhibition | Huskies surge in second half to down Longhorns UConn vs Syracuse takeaways: Seven observations from UConn women’s basketball’s win over Syracuse Why freshman Olivia Vukosa is ready: Geno Auriemma’s tough talk is a good sign for UConn’s Olivia Vukosa Popovic is outstanding again After a solid showing in her first exhibition game, Jovana Popovic once again showed that she isn’t your average freshman. The Serbian point guard played 36 minutes and scored 22 points on 7-of-11 shooting while grabbing seven rebounds and dishing out five assists. She hit all three of her shots from beyond the arc, hit 5-of-6 of her free throws and registered a plus-minus rating of +25. “The shots she makes are just shots you need when we really need her to make them,” Auriemma said. “She's calm and she's good.” How did the Huskies guard Booker? Most WNBA mock drafts have Texas forward Madison Booker as a consensus Top 3 pick in next year’s draft. So how did the Huskies fare guarding one of the nation’s elite scorers? On paper, Booker had an efficient scoring night, scoring 23 points on 11-of-17 shooting. But the stats don’t tell the whole story. UConn pulled away in the third quarter and held Booker to just four points in that period. Booker’s scoring didn’t lead to many opportunities to set up her teammates as she only logged one assist. The 6-foot-1 forward also never went to the free throw line in 30 minutes of play. “They spend a lot of their possession running Madison Booker off every kind of screen imaginable, and I think you've got to fight through all those, and you gotta work really hard,” Auriemma said. "It's a really difficult assignment.” Another Strong showing The reigning national player of the year has continued to show why she is regarded as the sport’s best player once again. Along with her 27 points, she added three rebounds, three assists and three blocks. She dueled with Booker all night and led the Huskies to a win. “It was our five against their five, so I just tried to stick to the game plan and support my team wherever I can,” Strong said. What has impressed Auriemma the most so far has been Strong’s leadership. “I think her voice carries a lot of weight,” Auriemma said. "I think she had it easy with Paige (Bueckers) and Kaitlyn Chen. This year, she's taking more ownership, more responsibility and the players listen.” Ziebell’s return Junior guard Allie Ziebell returned from an ankle injury that has kept her out for the last month. She played 21 minutes and scored eight points on 3-of-5 shooting from the field. She hit two of her three 3-point attempts. “I thought she did awesome,” senior guard Ashlynn Shade said of Ziebell. “I think she is so confident and comfortable with her game this season and this year in general. She came out and she contributed so much, and it's good to have her back out there with us.” Cheli update Redshirt sophomore guard Morgan Cheli was a surprising scratch from Monday’s game after she played in last week’s game against Syracuse. Auriemma did discuss the nature of Cheli’s injury and said she is “day-to-day.” This article originally appeared on The Bulletin: Five takeaways from UConn women’s basketball’s win over Texas

item.title: Giants can’t let one deep catch excuse a costly fumble
item.description: Oct 18, 2026; East Rutherford, New Jersey, USA; New York Giants wide receiver Charlie Jones (89) catches a kickoff against the New Orleans Saints during the third quarter at MetLife Stadium. Mandatory Credit: John Jones-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Charlie Jones caught two passes for 66 yards Sunday, including a 49-yard gain that helped drag the Giants back into a game they were losing badly. His offensive contribution deserves credit. I wouldn’t let it settle who handles the next kickoff. Earlier in the 34-27 loss to New Orleans, Jones lost a kickoff return that handed the Saints possession at New York’s 28. A useful receiver can still make a disastrous special-teams mistake, and the Giants need to evaluate those jobs separately. The Giants have other return experience Jones has averaged 24.2 yards on 11 kickoff returns this season. Tyrone Tracy Jr. has averaged 29.6 on seven, while Deonte Banks has two returns at an 18.5-yard average. Those are small samples with different opportunities, not a ranking that automatically picks the next returner. Oct 18, 2026; East Rutherford, New Jersey, USA; New York Giants wide receiver Charlie Jones (89) catches a pass against New Orleans Saints cornerback Quincy Riley (29) during the fourth quarter at MetLife Stadium. Mandatory Credit: John Jones-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They do establish that the Giants aren’t stuck with one player who has ever done the job. I would give the available alternatives a genuine competition in preparation for Houston rather than treat Jones’ return assignment as inseparable from his place in the passing offense. There is a complication with Tracy in particular: he’s had his own ball-security mistakes. His receiving and rushing responsibilities also have to be considered before adding another assignment. Making a change just to say someone was punished isn’t much of a plan. 0 What do you think? Post a comment. Jones’ two receptions were his first catches of the season. The 49-yarder was an encouraging contribution from a player who hadn’t been supplying offensive production, but two completions don’t tell us that he needs a major receiving role either. The reasonable outcome might be Jones remaining a reserve receiver while someone else gets the first opportunity on kickoffs. It might also be Jones keeping both jobs after a serious ball-security review. What shouldn’t happen is the late highlight being used to skip that review. The Giants’ broader defensive failures still count. New Orleans didn’t score 34 unanswered points because of one return alone. Giving an opponent a short field, though, is exactly the sort of avoidable mistake that makes every other weakness harder to survive. A clean week of return work would be a start for Jones. He should have to win that assignment on its own merits, even if the Giants keep finding a few useful routes for him on offense. Related Headlines JJ McCarthy should get the Giants’ next star

item.title: NFL fans think they have figured out Super Bowl halftime show after Star Wars announcement
item.description: Photo by Rick Stewart/Getty Images More and more clues are seemingly being shared ahead of February’s Super Bowl halftime show. Although it remains unclear as to which artist will be performing at SoFi Stadium, there are a number of possibilities being suggested as the event nears. There are still months of football to be played before the two competing teams are decided but work is already going into preparing the big event. On Monday, the NFL shared a post showcasing C-3PO and R2-D2 from the Star Wars series with the caption, ‘Coming soon on Super Bowl Sunday.’ With a number of high-profile musicians have already been linked to the Super Bowl halftime show but there may have been a twist that some NFL fans have already figured out. NFL fans react to Star Wars hint ahead of Super Bowl LXI The video shared by the NFL showed the two Star Wars characters having a conversation about the Super Bowl. “Where do you think you’re going? To the Super Bowl? We are going to the Super Bowl? Well, now that you ask, I am ready for some football,” said C-3PO. This has led to fans questioning what role in the Super Bowl the Star Wars franchise is going to play. ‘While I like Star Wars, I have a bad feeling about this. That, or this, is a weird way of saying the Cantina Band is going to be doing the halftime show,’ replied one fan. ‘Cantina Band Super Bowl Halftime performance?’ another like-minded fan said. The very end credit of the video showed a Super Bowl X Star Wars logo saying ‘Super Bowl Funday Football’ which could potentially suggest something other than the halftime show. However, some fans continued to link the possibilities together. ‘Just proves they don’t have a halftime performer yet 🤣 We usually know by now,’ replied another NFL fan. ‘A Cantina Band halftime performance would go insanely hard,’ added another. Next year will mark the 50th anniversary of Star Wars which make this one of the first collaborations the film franchise could pull off in 2027. ‘I just realised who’s going to be the halftime performer,’ another Star Wars fan replied. ‘Let’s gooooooo,’ said another. Read more: Jason Whitlock says Colts firing Chris Ballard is perfect opportunity to get Carlie Irsay-Gordon ‘off the sidelines’ Stephen A. Smith tells Jerry Jones to make big Cowboys decision before Halloween ‘I know Sean’ – Denver Broncos told they’d win the Super Bowl by making blockbuster trade

item.title: The SoCon title contenders
item.description: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - MARCH 20: Cole Bowser #6 of the Furman Paladins drives to the basket past Solo Ball #1 of the UConn Huskies during the second half during the first round of the 2026 NCAA Men's Basketball Tournament held at Xfinity Mobile Arena on March 20, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Ben Solomon/NCAA Photos via Getty Images) | NCAA Photos via Getty Images Furman 22-13, 10-8 SoCon/6 th in Regular-Season/2026 Tournament Champion When Stephen Croone and Devin Sibley helped power Furman to the Southern Conference title game as the No. 10 seed almost 12 years ago, few could have predicted the Paladins would have sustained that winning success to now become the SoCon’s standard torchbearer over the past decade. But that is exactly what has transpired with two NCAA Tournament appearances, two NIT appearances, a top-25 ranking, and 245 wins later, the Paladins are now a program considered among the mid-major elite, year-in and year-out. Furman now looks to become the first team since the 2014 and ’15 SoCon Tournament champion Wofford Terriers to win back-to-back SoCon titles. In a league like the SoCon, it’s become increasingly tougher to win back-to-back titles. The Paladins welcome back a healthy amount of talent from that team that lifted the title just last season, but there are some significant losses, too. Furman’s lone All-SoCon performer — Alex Wilkins — who led the team by averaging 17.4 PPG as a true freshman last season has moved on to the University of Kentucky. Wilkins was a freshman phenom who took the SoCon by storm last season, and it was little surprise that he was named the Southern Conference MVP, performing at such a high level in the semifinal round of the tournament, as he finished that contest with 34 points in the 81-75 win over UNCG. The Mattapan, Mass., native connected on 10-of-17 shots from the field, including 4-of-7 from 3-point range. Tom House was also a key component of the title run last season, posting 13 points in the championship game, while Cooper Bowser made a strong case for the tournament’s Most Outstanding Player honor, as he added 21 points on a near-flawless 9-of-12 shooting performance for the game. With the prospect of Furman’s three most important players offensively in the tournament having potentially moved on, it makes for an interesting transition to the 2026-27 season. Bowser transferred to Arkansas and joins Wilkins in the SEC. Eddrin Bronson has moved on and will be a key piece for Ed Conroy’s The Citadel Bulldogs next season, while Asa Thomas, who spent one season at Furman after transferring in from Clemson, has transferred to be closer to his home state of Illinois, as he will suit up for the Illinois-Chicago Flames next season. Ben Vander Wal graduated, and House remains in limbo, as he awaits a court ruling for the 2022-23 freshman class, as he is part of a class-action lawsuit seeking a fifth year of eligibility. (Photo by Ben Solomon/NCAA Photos via Getty Images) | NCAA Photos via Getty Images Furman 22-13, 10-8 SoCon/6 th in Regular-Season/2026 Tournament Champion When Stephen Croone and Devin Sibley helped power Furman to the Southern Conference title game as the No. 10 seed almost 12 years ago, few could have predicted the Paladins would have sustained that winning success to now become the SoCon’s standard torchbearer over the past decade. But that is exactly what has transpired with two NCAA Tournament appearances, two NIT appearances, a top-25 ranking, and 245 wins later, the Paladins are now a program considered among the mid-major elite, year-in and year-out. Furman now looks to become the first team since the 2014 and ’15 SoCon Tournament champion Wofford Terriers to win back-to-back SoCon titles. In a league like the SoCon, it’s become increasingly tougher to win back-to-back titles. The Paladins welcome back a healthy amount of talent from that team that lifted the title just last season, but there are some significant losses, too. Furman’s lone All-SoCon performer — Alex Wilkins — who led the team by averaging 17.4 PPG as a true freshman last season has moved on to the University of Kentucky. Wilkins was a freshman phenom who took the SoCon by storm last season, and it was little surprise that he was named the Southern Conference MVP, performing at such a high level in the semifinal round of the tournament, as he finished that contest with 34 points in the 81-75 win over UNCG. The Mattapan, Mass., native connected on 10-of-17 shots from the field, including 4-of-7 from 3-point range. Tom House was also a key component of the title run last season, posting 13 points in the championship game, while Cooper Bowser made a strong case for the tournament’s Most Outstanding Player honor, as he added 21 points on a near-flawless 9-of-12 shooting performance for the game. With the prospect of Furman’s three most important players offensively in the tournament having potentially moved on, it makes for an interesting transition to the 2026-27 season. Bowser transferred to Arkansas and joins Wilkins in the SEC. Eddrin Bronson has moved on and will be a key piece for Ed Conroy’s The Citadel Bulldogs next season, while Asa Thomas, who spent one season at Furman after transferring in from Clemson, has transferred to be closer to his home state of Illinois, as he will suit up for the Illinois-Chicago Flames next season. Ben Vander Wal graduated, and House remains in limbo, as he awaits a court ruling for the 2022-23 freshman class, as he is part of a class-action lawsuit seeking a fifth year of eligibility. In 6-foot-11 forward Charles Johnston’s case, in the state of California, he was granted a temporary restraining order, as part of the class-action lawsuit in that state, and as of mid-September, Johnston is eligible to play in 2026-27. As a result of a stay in Ohio, House remains ineligible for that extra fifth year in mid-September. Both are currently enrolled in graduate courses at Furman for the 2026-27 school year. Should Furman get one or both back this season, it could have a significant impact on how the season pans out for head coach Bob Richey’s Paladins. Richey, who enters his 10 th year as the head coach, now has over 200 wins at Furman, reaching that total in Furman’s Senior Night, 72-51, win over The Citadel. He sits at 203 total wins as the head coach as we enter the 2026-27 season. Though the Paladins lose potentially their top seven scorers from last season, Furman has some key pieces returning from a year ago, including a trio of players who played significant roles as freshmen last season: Cole Bowser (5.2 PPG, 5.3 RPG), Collin O’Neal (2.9 PPG, 1.4 RPG) and Abijah Franklin (4.4 PPG, 1.8 RPG). O’Neal suffered an knee injury in a home win over Harvard in December, which kept him out for a large portion of the season. O’Neal had been one of Furman’s top performers off the bench prior to his injury and was able to enjoy his best performance in Furman’s 72-65 loss to Illinois State in the Old Spice Classic’s Imagination Bracket Championship game in Kissimmee, Fla., last season. He connected on all four of his 3-pointers and finished with 12 points off the bench in the Furman loss. Bowser was expected to redshirt the entire season, but with some significant injuries beginning to mount, including a foot injury to his brother Cooper Bowser, had his redshirt be removed, and he became a significant role player in the front court as the season progressed. Bowser became useful as a pick-and-pop guy from the perimeter, as well as on the defensive end of the floor. The younger Bowser saw action in 20 games, including making six starts. He was a significant factor in Furman’s championship win over East Tennessee State last March, as he finished with four points, four rebounds and blocked a pair of shots off the bench. Bowser proved to be a solid threat for the Paladins from the perimeter, as he connected on 36% (14-of-39) from 3-point range, and was also effective overall from the field, connecting on 46% of his shots from the field. Bowser is also a solid defender on the perimeter for the Paladins, and he will once again be an x-factor this season for the Paladins. He has all-conference talent. Franklin, who should be another young player who comes into his own, especially now that he is no longer playing in the shadow of Wilkins. The former Wren HS standout was a pure scorer during his prep career and is expected to be one of several scoring options for the Paladins this coming season, and I expect he will emerge as one of the three or four double-figure scorers the Paladins will feature this season. Franklin finished the season shooting 29.8% (14-of-47) and shot 63.6% (21-of-33) from the free-throw line, as well as connecting at a 35.4% (35-of-99) clip from the field. Molnar is a gritty player who could add some depth underneath, while being an added force on the glass on both ends. Molnar is also a decent defender, and he’s seen his shot improve significantly this season. In his final season with the Catamounts, Kell averaged 13.6 PPG and 4.8 RPG. item.title: Aston Villa defender back in training – but Emery confirms injury blows ahead of Viking game
item.description: Aston Villa defender back in training – but Emery confirms injury blows ahead of Viking game Ian Maatsen has returned to Aston Villa training ahead of Wednesday’s Champions League clash with Viking, but Johan Manzambi and Aaron Wan-Bissaka will both miss the game. Maatsen has been sidelined since Villa’s Premier League meeting with Nottingham Forest in mid-September but is now back working with his team-mates at Bodymoor Heath. “Coming back and joining us is Ian Maatsen,” Villa boss Unai Emery said. “He’s joined us and is training with us this week.” There was less positive news on Manzambi, who picked up a minor issue in Saturday’s 1-0 win over Newcastle United. “Manzambi has a small injury,” Emery said. “He’s not available for tomorrow.” Wan-Bissaka also suffered an injury at St James’ Park and is expected to be sidelined for three to four weeks. “Aaron has an injury as well,” Emery added. “More or less we expect three or four weeks.” Matteo Ruggeri and Amadou Onana also remain unavailable. “We are accepting of the injuries we had before,” Emery said. “So many players we had injured in our process here and now we’re still having some, like Onana for a long time, like Matteo for more or less two months. “We have enough players, no excuses, and tomorrow we’ll find solutions in case we need to get our performance, of course, collectively and individually in each position.”

item.title: “Let the team down and he let me down”: Ten Hag revisits Ronaldo fallout with damning unprofessionalism claim
item.description: “Let the team down and he let me down”: Ten Hag revisits Ronaldo fallout with damning unprofessionalism claim Former Manchester United head coach Erik ten Hag has reignited his bitter feud with Cristiano Ronaldo by accusing him of lacking professionalism. Spat Ten Hag infamously clashed with Ronaldo during his stint at United, as the pair failed to see eye to eye. There were occasions when the Dutch coach left Ronaldo out of the squad, and eventually the frustration boiled over, with Ronaldo storming out of the stadium in fury. Ronaldo then conducted a controversial interview with broadcaster Piers Morgan, in which he accused Ten Hag of disrespecting him. The five-time Ballon d’Or winner also criticised his teammates and even the owners for neglecting the club over the years. United responded by terminating Ronaldo’s contract and paving the way for him to move to the Saudi Pro League. Since then, the saga has been frequently revisited, with the prevailing perception that Ten Hag did not favour Ronaldo because of his unwillingness to press and perform defensive duties for the team. Now technical director at Twente, Ten Hag has all but confirmed this, criticising Ronaldo’s poor preparation and effort while revealing that the forward attempted to influence his teammates during training. Damning revelation Ten Hag told Laurie Whitwell of The Athletic , “He let the team down, and he let me down, because we planned with him. I flew out to Portugal to speak with him about what I was aiming for before I came to United. Obviously, he’s one of the best in football history. I respected him a lot.” “But at that time, as a manager, I had to make a rational decision and keep the players I admire in.” Ten Hag noted that Ronaldo pulled out of training altogether, refused to push his heart rate to the required level, and when he did deign to train, completed only two of the three laps of the infamous punishment run Ten Hag ordered after the Brentford humiliation in August 2022. “I confronted him with this. Many times I say, ‘Ronnie, everyone wants to work for you to bring you in the right position, but if you can’t bring yourself in the box, you can’t score’. He was not capable to do this.” “It’s the wrong idea to put this to me that I expected him to do the pressing, that he’s exhausted. But he couldn’t. He ran neither in possession nor out of possession. The reason was because he didn’t prepare himself.” “Every top team has to embrace the top player, but the top player has to work for the team. He was telling the players, ‘Save your legs at the training’. I understand it when you are top fit; you have sessions, you can save the legs. But first you have to train yourself to get into the right fitness levels.” Ten Hag lifted the FA Cup and Carabao Cup during his time at United.

item.title: Barcelona coach’s key role in developing La Masia starlet called up for PSG clash
item.description: Barcelona coach’s key role in developing La Masia starlet called up for PSG clash Barcelona head to Paris to take on PSG with a much-depleted defence following injuries to Jules Kounde and Eric Garcia. The Catalan giants were already without the services of Andreas Christensen, and these latest two injuries have complicated Hansi Flick’s plans. As always, Barça have turned to La Masia during a time of crisis, and Alex Campos has received his first senior call-up against PSG. Interestingly, one member of Hansi Flick’s coaching staff has played a particularly important role in the youngster’s journey to the first team. According to SPORT , Flick’s assistant Arnau Blanco has known Campos since 2019 and was involved in both his recruitment and development at La Masia . Arnau Blanco’s long-standing connection with Alex Campos Blanco first spotted Campos while working alongside Albert Puig in Barcelona’s Infantil B set-up. The young defender was playing for Atletic Segre, and both coaches quickly recognised his potential. Instead of forcing his move to Barcelona immediately, they chose a more unconventional route. The coaches allowed him to stay at his club and playing there while allowing him to train with La Masia . Alex Campos played a key role in the development of Barcelona starlet. (Picture credit: Instagram/@aleexcampos_) He eventually joined Barcelona in 2021, initially developing as a central defender despite previously impressing in midfield. Their paths crossed again during the 2023-24 season, when Blanco coached Campos in Barcelona’s Cadete A. The defender started all 30 league matches that campaign, establishing himself as a crucial player in a successful youth team. Why Blanco’s influence matters ahead of PSG Campos has continued progressing under Juliano Belletti at Barça Atletic, where his performances alongside Hafiz Gariba have strengthened his reputation. The youngster stands out for his composure, passing ability and confidence when building attacks from defence. Although naturally right-footed, he can operate on either side of central defence, potentially making him a useful partner for Pau Cubarsi. Alex Campos could receive his first minutes for Barcelona against PSG (Photo courtesy: FC Barcelona official website) His defensive prowess has increased significantly, adding greater reliability to his ability on the ball. With Eric, Kounde and Christensen unavailable, Campos is now with the team in Paris and could even make his first-team debut during the game. Blanco’s presence could now become particularly valuable. Having followed the defender’s development for years, he could help with his integration into the first team. Gerard Martin is not 100 percent fit coming into this game, and the Spaniard may not be able to play 90 minutes against PSG. item.title: Man Utd on alert as EPL club ‘forced’ to sell 62-goal star at a discount in January
item.description: Man Utd on alert as EPL club ‘forced’ to sell 62-goal star at a discount in January Manchester United have reportedly been presented with a golden opportunity to sign their longtime target Jean-Philippe Mateta. The Frenchman has been on Jason Wilcox’s watchlist at least since his memorable 2024/25 campaign, when he led Crystal Palace’s charge towards FA Cup glory. In the end, the Red Devils opted to sign the younger Benjamin Sesko from RB Leipzig on a deal worth £72 million. Man Utd directors ready to reinforce the attack in January (Photo by Richard Heathcote/Getty Images) While United do not necessarily regret recruiting Sesko, who had a decent first campaign in England, his lengthy absence has been harming the team’s chances this season, especially amid the lack of a natural replacement. In August, the 23-year-old made his return from a serious shin injury, only to suffer a fresh setback a few weeks later. Experts suggest Sesko could remain on the sidelines for a while . According to talkSPORT journalist Alex Crook, Man Utd’s hierarchy realise they should have done more on the market in the summer to strengthen the attack. Therefore, Wilcox and Co. are ready to pounce on any inviting opportunities in January. The source reveals that Mateta could be the ideal solution, as Palace could be ‘forced’ to place him on the market. The 29-year-old’s contract will expire in June, and he has no desire to pen an extension. Therefore, the Eagles would be ready to cash in on the big striker in January, albeit at a discount. Does signing Mateta make sense for Man United? (Photo by Lewis Storey/Getty Images) Mateta has been plying his trade at Selhurst Park since 2021, so it’s past time for him to embark on a new career chapter. Palace have already moved on by signing Jørgen Strand Larsen. They tried to sell the Frenchman last January, but AC Milan pulled out after a failed medical on deadline day. This season, the bomber missed the first two months due to a hamstring injury, but he made his return to action in the 0-5 defeat to Brighton on Sunday. In Mateta, Man Utd would have an EPL-proven centre-forward with international experience. His big frame and ability to bring teammates into the play render him an ideal alternative for Sesko in Michael Carrick’s system. However, INEOS wouldn’t want to add another injury-riddled striker to their ranks. Hence, the directors must make sure he has overcome all of the physical issues that hampered his momentum in recent campaigns before bringing him to Old Trafford. item.title: UEFA Champions League Preview: Como vs Manchester United – Team News, Lineups & Prediction
item.description: UEFA Champions League Preview: Como vs Manchester United – Team News, Lineups & Prediction Arguably the biggest night in the history of the Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium pits Como against Manchester United in a high-stakes UEFA Champions League showdown. Wednesday’s clash finds two teams in starkly contrasting circumstances. Como produced another emphatic performance at the weekend, beating Fiorentina 3-1 in Tuscany to end a three-game winless streak in all competitions (D1, L2). That underwhelming run featured a 3-2 defeat at Feyenoord in their last Champions League outing, which canceled out their heroics from matchday one. It was a dream European debut for Cesc Fabregas’ side as they humbled RB Leipzig 4-1 at this venue, putting themselves in a position to become the first Serie A team since Lazio in 1999/2000 to win their first two Champions League home matches. However, Lariani should know better than to take anything for granted against the three-time European champions. Glory days are long gone at Old Trafford, but Como can ill afford to underestimate Manchester United. Under-fire boss Michael Carrick is standing on the precipice of an expulsion amid the Red Devils’ dreadful start. They’ve won just two of their ten competitive games in 2026/27 so far (D4, L4) and are currently on a six-game winless streak in all competitions. Desperate to end their longest such run since 2019, Man Utd will be out to make amends for a 2-0 defeat at Atletico Madrid last week and get their faltering Champions League campaign back on track. Match Preview Como With high-profile clashes against high-flying La Liga leaders Barcelona and reigning European champions Paris Saint-Germain still yet to come, Como must make the most out of their next few Champions League outings, including this one. Playing at the Sinigaglia should inspire confidence in Fabregas’ camp, given that the Lariani have only lost one home match since February (W6, D3). It’s also worth noting that they won their first two home games this season by an aggregate score of 6-2 before being held to a frustrating scoreless draw by a 10-man Roma side last time out. Another dull contest is unlikely to take place on Wednesday, especially considering the fact that three of Como’s last four fixtures have featured at least two first-half goals. Meanwhile, if there’s a man aware of the gravity of the threat Man Utd could pose, it’s Fabregas. The former Arsenal, Barcelona, and Chelsea star faced the Red Devils 24 times during his illustrious playing career. He’s likely to put his side’s fate into the hands of in-form striker Tasos Douvikas, who has scored in both Champions League appearances this term. However, Lariani should know better than to take anything for granted against the three-time European champions. Glory days are long gone at Old Trafford, but Como can ill afford to underestimate Manchester United. Under-fire boss Michael Carrick is standing on the precipice of an expulsion amid the Red Devils’ dreadful start. They’ve won just two of their ten competitive games in 2026/27 so far (D4, L4) and are currently on a six-game winless streak in all competitions. Desperate to end their longest such run since 2019, Man Utd will be out to make amends for a 2-0 defeat at Atletico Madrid last week and get their faltering Champions League campaign back on track. Match Preview Como With high-profile clashes against high-flying La Liga leaders Barcelona and reigning European champions Paris Saint-Germain still yet to come, Como must make the most out of their next few Champions League outings, including this one. Playing at the Sinigaglia should inspire confidence in Fabregas’ camp, given that the Lariani have only lost one home match since February (W6, D3). It’s also worth noting that they won their first two home games this season by an aggregate score of 6-2 before being held to a frustrating scoreless draw by a 10-man Roma side last time out. Another dull contest is unlikely to take place on Wednesday, especially considering the fact that three of Como’s last four fixtures have featured at least two first-half goals. Meanwhile, if there’s a man aware of the gravity of the threat Man Utd could pose, it’s Fabregas. The former Arsenal, Barcelona, and Chelsea star faced the Red Devils 24 times during his illustrious playing career. He’s likely to put his side’s fate into the hands of in-form striker Tasos Douvikas, who has scored in both Champions League appearances this term. Manchester United Anything other than a win in Italy could spell the end of Carrick’s tenure at the Theatre of Dreams, but Man Utd’s recent continental struggles paint a bleak picture for the former midfielder. Atletico Madrid inflicted United’s sixth defeat across their last nine Champions League matches (D3, L6), overshadowing their 4-0 victory over Sabah Baku on the opening matchday. Furthermore, the Red Devils have traveled poorly of late, picking up just one win in their last ten Champions League away games (D3, L6). Even the most optimistic Man Utd fans would not dare to dream big here, knowing the 20-time English champions have yet to win a competitive fixture on the road this season (D3, L2). As if that’s not ominous enough, the visitors have conceded two or more goals in eight of their last ten Champions League away outings, perhaps best summarising their travel sickness. Against this backdrop, a six-game unbeaten away run against Italian opposition (W3, D3), stretching back to 2007, offers a glimmer of hope to Carrick that he could dodge the bullet tomorrow. Team News Apart from the injured Assane Diao, Como must also perform late checks on Trevoh Chalobah and Moise Kean, who are both at risk of missing this showdown due to minor fitness problems. Even if deemed fit, Kean would likely start on the bench, with Douvikas expected to lead the line alongside Nico Paz and Martin Baturina. Meanwhile, Man Utd are still without former Serie A star Patrick Dorgu and Slovenian striker Benjamin Sesko. Leny Yoro is also unavailable for selection after being sent off against Atletico Madrid. Lisandro Martinez is likely to take the Frenchman’s place in the starting lineup and partner up with Harry Maguire at the heart of Carrick’s defense. Como vs Manchester United Potential Starting Lineups Como (4-2-3-1): Butez; Couto, Chalobah, Ramon, Valle; Milla, Da Cunha; J Rodriguez, Paz, Baturina; Douvikas. Manchester United (4-2-3-1): Lammens; Mazraoui, Maguire, Martinez, Dalot; Santos, Baleba; Amad, Tielemans, Fernandes; Mbeumo. Como vs Manchester United Prediction Despite Man Utd’s rough patch, it’s impossible to write the Red Devils out of this one before kickoff. A win would significantly increase Como’s chances of reaching the knockout stages, but we expect the teams to share the spoils in their first-ever meeting.

item.title: From clay to grass: record FIFA funding boosts emerging nations
item.description: From clay to grass: record FIFA funding boosts emerging nations Through a significant increase in funding and greater access to tournaments, developing football markets such as Mauritania, Bangladesh and Bhutan are building strong, lasting sporting structures. For many emerging football nations, FIFA is the main, if not the only, reliable source of sporting revenue. Recent financial figures and strategic shifts point to a concerted effort by world football's governing body to build sustainable structures in these markets, focusing on three pillars: financial support, talent development and greater access to tournaments. The financial growth is clear. Under the FIFA Forward programme, funding for each member association has risen from $3.8 million in the 2016-2018 cycle to $8 million in the current 2023-2026 cycle. A new proposal on the table for 2027-2030 aims to provide associations with a total of $25 million each. Ahmed Yahya, president of the Mauritanian Football Federation, highlighted the practical impact of these figures following a recent FIFA Council meeting. "These financial resources allow today's young people to play on real grass pitches rather than rocky or dirt surfaces, and that is what really matters," Yahya explained. He also stressed the fundamental importance of equal funding and voting rights for all nations. "For us, equality is what defines FIFA today. Gianni Infantino is taking football forward worldwide... The majority want him to stay." Crucially, this financial support goes hand in hand with the "FIFA Talent Development Scheme" and the expansion of youth tournaments. By helping associations identify and nurture talent while offering more opportunities to showcase it on the global stage, FIFA is seeking to create a system in which football can become a genuine career in developing regions. In Bangladesh, this combined strategy is delivering tangible results. Tabith Awal, president of the Bangladesh Football Federation, recalled recent milestones, including a historic victory over San Marino and an invitation to the FIFA ASEAN Cup. "We have made use of many of FIFA's valuable projects, from the Arena programme to Forward, to genuinely develop a football culture in our country," Awal said. Awal also praised the current administration's approach to governance, noting that Infantino "continues to extend a hand of friendship" even amid disagreements at leadership level. A recent stop in Dhaka by the FIFA president allowed local officials to demonstrate exactly how international funding is being used on the ground. This strategy of global outreach extends to Bhutan, which recently welcomed a FIFA president to the country for the first time in its history. The visit underscored the organisation's aim of maintaining direct contact with all member associations, regardless of their size, and gave local leaders an opportunity to plan for the future.
