item.content:encoded: From clay to grass: record FIFA funding boosts emerging nations Through a significant increase in funding and greater access to tournaments, developing football markets such as Mauritania, Bangladesh and Bhutan are building strong, lasting sporting structures. For many emerging football nations, FIFA is the main, if not the only, reliable source of sporting revenue. Recent financial figures and strategic shifts point to a concerted effort by world football's governing body to build sustainable structures in these markets, focusing on three pillars: financial support, talent development and greater access to tournaments. The financial growth is clear. Under the FIFA Forward programme, funding for each member association has risen from $3.8 million in the 2016-2018 cycle to $8 million in the current 2023-2026 cycle. A new proposal on the table for 2027-2030 aims to provide associations with a total of $25 million each. Ahmed Yahya, president of the Mauritanian Football Federation, highlighted the practical impact of these figures following a recent FIFA Council meeting. "These financial resources allow today's young people to play on real grass pitches rather than rocky or dirt surfaces, and that is what really matters," Yahya explained. He also stressed the fundamental importance of equal funding and voting rights for all nations. "For us, equality is what defines FIFA today. Gianni Infantino is taking football forward worldwide... The majority want him to stay." Crucially, this financial support goes hand in hand with the "FIFA Talent Development Scheme" and the expansion of youth tournaments. By helping associations identify and nurture talent while offering more opportunities to showcase it on the global stage, FIFA is seeking to create a system in which football can become a genuine career in developing regions. In Bangladesh, this combined strategy is delivering tangible results. Tabith Awal, president of the Bangladesh Football Federation, recalled recent milestones, including a historic victory over San Marino and an invitation to the FIFA ASEAN Cup. "We have made use of many of FIFA's valuable projects, from the Arena programme to Forward, to genuinely develop a football culture in our country," Awal said. Awal also praised the current administration's approach to governance, noting that Infantino "continues to extend a hand of friendship" even amid disagreements at leadership level. A recent stop in Dhaka by the FIFA president allowed local officials to demonstrate exactly how international funding is being used on the ground. This strategy of global outreach extends to Bhutan, which recently welcomed a FIFA president to the country for the first time in its history. The visit underscored the organisation's aim of maintaining direct contact with all member associations, regardless of their size, and gave local leaders an opportunity to plan for the future. Dasho Ugen Tsechup, president of the Bhutan Football Federation (BFF), used the historic visit to outline ambitious initiatives. "Because of his busy schedule, time was limited. But our discussions were concise and to the point," Ugen Tsechup explained. "With FIFA's assistance, so much more can now be done in Bhutan." He then outlined a comprehensive development plan that includes the Rama project (a school and academy for boys and girls), the commercial redevelopment of existing football facilities at Changjiji and GMC, and the construction of a new stadium in Paro. Asked to name the single project from the Infantino era of which he was most proud, Ugen Tsechup declined to choose, stressing the cumulative effect of sustained support. "I cannot pick just one, because every single investment has made an important contribution to the development of football in Bhutan," he said. "The headquarters, which gave us independence... the academy, the facilities, the pitches, the mini-pitches, the futsal courts: every aspect of infrastructure development supported by FIFA has been a milestone for our federation." These targeted investments are having a profound human impact, especially in women's football. Pema Choden Tshering, captain of Bhutan's women's national team, has experienced this transformation firsthand, starting at grassroots level. "I grew up playing on dusty pitches. Now I have the opportunity to play on artificial turf and natural grass pitches through my international experiences," Tshering noted. She pointed to the creation of a girls' academy in Gelephu—where more than 60 girls train regularly throughout the year—as a direct result of improved facilities. Tshering also thanked the FIFA Forward programme for funding crucial trips that allow the team to compete internationally. "This has given the girls so many opportunities to grow, not just as players, but as people," she added. With national team players now securing contracts abroad, Tshering is optimistic: "I hope this inspires the young girls of the future and encourages parents to let more girls play the sport." While elite European football dominates media headlines, the institutional reality for countries such as Mauritania, Bangladesh and Bhutan is that structured, sustained investment is creating solid new foundations. By combining reliable funding, clear pathways for talent and grassroots infrastructure, FIFA is laying the groundwork needed for world football to grow equitably. item.title: Adam Silver sees the positives of having parity in the NBA with 8 champions in 8 seasons
item.description: Adam Silver sees the positives of having parity in the NBA with 8 champions in 8 seasons originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Ever since the Golden State Warriors repeated as champions in 2017 and 2018, no team has won two titles in a row. In fact, there have been eight different champions since the 2018 Finals, with the most recent champion being the New York Knicks , who won their first title in 52 seasons. Leading up to the 2026-27 NBA season's opening day, League Commissioner Adam Silver went on Good Morning America to talk about the upcoming season. He spoke about the parity with all the teams winning championships, and the positives that stem from it. NBA Commissioner Adam Silver speaks on why parity is meaningful for the league Back when the Warriors repeated back in 2017 and 2018, the NBA was extremely different from what it is today. There were plenty of teams that were trying to be competitive, but they just couldn't beat the dominant teams, which were the Warriors and the Cleveland Cavaliers at the time. Before them were the Miami Heat , the San Antonio Spurs , and the Los Angeles Lakers . All those teams won multiple championships during their heyday, and the Heat and the Lakers even had repeats. That has not happened over the past decade, which just goes to show the quality of teams around the NBA. MORE: NBA experts do not think the New York Knicks will repeat as champions While some people might see this as a negative, Silver does not see that perspective at all. He loves what he is seeing from the league's parity, which is a big deal for the NBA and the chances of teams winning championships even if they're not from the biggest of markets. "It says so much about the level of competition and the parity in this league. It's why I think this is one of the most anticipated seasons because there are so many teams that believe they have a shot this year. When you add that global pool of talent, for people who just love basketball, you can watch any game in any night; there's always something to see," Silver said on Good Morning America about the league's level of competition . It is hard to argue against Silver's point, but there will be people who will talk about how a certain team dominating would be good for narratives. There will come a time when a team repeats as champions, but at the moment, the parity era in the NBA has led to the sport shining even more due to the quality of basketball around the league. item.title: Leeds sign prop Salabio as McCormack extends deal
item.description: Hugo Salabio made 12 appearances for Hull FC in 2026 [swpix.com] Leeds Rhinos have signed prop Hugo Salabio on a one-year deal. The 26-year-old France international left Hull FC at the end of the season after 18 appearances in two years. "Leeds is a massive club with a great history, and I've always admired the team and the supporters," he told the club website. Meanwhile, full-back Fergus McCormack has signed a new three-year contract. The 20-year-old made his debut for the Rhinos against Widnes in the Challenge Cup in February. He made three Super League appearances in May and June before injuries gave him the chance to start in the play-off semi-final defeat by Warrington last month.

item.description: Afghanistan and Bangladesh meet in Abu Dhabi on Wednesday with the a place in the tri-series final riding on the result. Afghanistan lead the table after beating Zimbabwe by 158 runs, with Sediqullah Atal making 102 and Rashid Khan taking four for 17. Bangladesh sit bottom after being bowled out for 172 against Zimbabwe while chasing 271 and they must win by roughly 40 runs if batting first, or chase in fewer overs, to go through. Afghanistan vs. Bangladesh 3rd ODI prediction: Who will win? Afghanistan have won the last four meetings against Bangladesh, including a 3-0 sweep in Abu Dhabi last October. Conditions also suit them. Sharjah averages 223 for the first innings and 190 for the second, and the pitch grips later under lights, so they will want to bat first with Zadran and Atal. Bangladesh have to win big, which could push them into reckless cricket, and Mehidy's fever is a worry. The one risk is Afghanistan easing off after beating Zimbabwe. item.title: Dream's Angel Reese is on pace to set Finals mark not seen since Shaquille O'Neal
item.description: Dream's Angel Reese is on pace to set Finals mark not seen since Shaquille O'Neal originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Through two games of the 2026 WNBA Finals, Angel Reese is averaging 22 points and 14 rebounds per game. It's a window into how her first-ever Finals could prove historic. Reese laid waste to the Golden State Valkyries ' vaunted defense on Monday, dropping a 30-point, 16-rebound double-double as she led the Atlanta Dream to their first-ever victory in the championship series. MORE : Angel Reese refused to let the Dream lose Game 2 of the WNBA Finals In the 79-65 win at San Francisco's Chase Center, Reese shot 10-of-16 from the field, following up her 5-of-11 shooting night from Saturday's Game 1 defeat. That means Reese is shooting 55 percent for the series while averaging better than 20 points per game. If she maintains that pace, she would be the youngest player to achieve those figures in the Finals since Shaquille O'Neal did so for the Orlando Magic in 1995. Angel Reese is on pace to be the youngest player to average 20+ PPG on 55% FG in the Finals since Shaq in 1995. https://t.co/U3mW1YLIY9 — Real App (@realapp) October 20, 2026 Perhaps it's a bad omen for Reese that O'Neal's Magic lost the Finals in 1995, suffering a four-game sweep at the hands of the Houston Rockets. But if Reese's young career has taught us anything, it's that any expectations or preconceived notions should be checked at the door. item.title: Ava Watson: Ohio State women’s basketball 2026-27 player preview
item.description: Ohio State Buckeyes guard Ava Watson (5) reacts in the second half of the NCAA basketball game against the Norfolk State Spartans at Value City Arena on Thursday, Dec. 18, 2025 in Columbus, Ohio. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Ohio State women’s basketball begins competitive games on Nov. 2 against the University of Illinois Chicago. When the Buckeyes take the court, there will not be too many changes in the available players for head coach Kevin McGuff’s side. Of the regular starting five, four players return including point guard Jaloni Cambridge, guard Kennedy Cambridge and bigs Elsa Lemmilä and Kylee Kitts. A big question surrounding those four is who steps into the shooting guard role, vacated by Chance Gray who had a career season in her final collegiate year. The start of Land-Grant Holy Land’s player preview series is the athlete most likely to take up that role — guard Ava Watson . After two seasons of mixed results, Watson’s third year gives her a clear path to being the Buckeyes’ fifth starter. How will Watson fill that role? Where is the junior’s focus headed into the 2026-27 season? item.content:encoded: Ohio State Buckeyes guard Ava Watson (5) reacts in the second half of the NCAA basketball game against the Norfolk State Spartans at Value City Arena on Thursday, Dec. 18, 2025 in Columbus, Ohio. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Ohio State women’s basketball begins competitive games on Nov. 2 against the University of Illinois Chicago. When the Buckeyes take the court, there will not be too many changes in the available players for head coach Kevin McGuff’s side. Of the regular starting five, four players return including point guard Jaloni Cambridge, guard Kennedy Cambridge and bigs Elsa Lemmilä and Kylee Kitts. A big question surrounding those four is who steps into the shooting guard role, vacated by Chance Gray who had a career season in her final collegiate year. The start of Land-Grant Holy Land’s player preview series is the athlete most likely to take up that role — guard Ava Watson . After two seasons of mixed results, Watson’s third year gives her a clear path to being the Buckeyes’ fifth starter. How will Watson fill that role? Where is the junior’s focus headed into the 2026-27 season? Name: Ava Watson Position: Guard Class: Junior High School: Buford High School (Buford, Georgia) 2025-26 Stats: 7.2 ppg, 2.2 rpg, 2.3 apg, 40.3 FG%, 35.6 FG%, 90.0 FT% Last Season To say that Watson was not a starter last season is not entirely true. Watson was one of only six Buckeyes who started at least 10 games but the guard’s path came due to injury. When Kitts suffered an injury against the TCU Horned Frogs on Jan 19, 2026, Watson stepped into the starting rotation and kept it through the final game of the season, in the Second Round of the NCAA Tournament. Watson played the fifth most minutes on the team and was second on the team with two steals per game, behind only Kennedy Cambridge who led the conference with 3.7 takeaways per contest. Throughout her 32 appearances, Watson had at least five steals in seven different games, plus a career high seven steals against Northern Kentucky and Niagara. Against stiffer competition in the Big Ten, Watson had six in her first collegiate start, up against the Indiana Hoosiers. Offensively, Waton’s 7.2 points per game was a career high, but that is in comparison to 25 appearances and no starts in her freshman season. Once Watson made the starting five, the guard scored double-digit points on six different occasions. On Nov. 26, when the West Virginia Mountaineers forced most of the starting lineup to foul out, Watson had 4 points, 3 steals and 2 assists in the fourth quarter. That stat line included an assist on the game-winning shot and the then sophomore hit the final two free throws of the game to secure the win. It was moments like that and more that helped Watson earn more of McGuff’s trust. It showed at the start of Watson’s jump in minutes when the Buckeyes faced TCU. Watson went head-to-head against guard Olivia Miles, who recently won the WNBA Rookie of the Year award in her first year with the Minnesota Lynx. In that 71-69 Buckeye victory, Miles gave the ball away four times. What to Expect Like many young college players who join a Power Four program and go from being the big fish in high school to a small fish in an ocean at the collegiate level, Watson admitted that her first two seasons lacked one specific area. “The past two years, I had zero confidence just within myself, and that’s never something that I’ve dealt with ever,” Watson told reporters. To work on it, Watson worked with her dad, Ohio State coaches and her guard group in the offseason to build on that confidence. That did not always show on the court with a small sample size of moments off the bench but this season Ohio State needs more from the guard. Watson knows this and has prepared in the offseason as if the starting shooting guard role now belongs to her. Specifically, on the offensive side of the ball. “My sole focus was defense,” said Watson. “This year, being my third season, I’ve kind of earned it, where I can go out there and kind of just be free and help my teammates in other ways, not just defense.” Gray was only one of two Buckeyes to average at least 10 points per game during the 25-26 season. The guard had a career high 14.7 points per game, hit a team high 2.4 three-point shots per game and at a personal best 40.5% from beyond the arc. “Now that Chance is leaving, that leaves me a little bit more room to shoot because she left. She gave us a lot, so I got to fill some shoes,” said Watson. That puts pressure on the guard, but the defensive work shown over the previous two seasons shows how important Watson is in the current window of Ohio State women’s basketball. Prediction The first true test for Watson — and the Buckeyes — comes quickly. On Nov. 12, the UConn Huskies descend on the Schottenstein Center after star forward Sarah Strong had a career day against Ohio State last year in Connecticut. That gives Watson three regular season games to work on that offensive improvement in game speed. Even though they all come against mid-major sides, the Buckeyes can build momentum. Watson played with the Cambridges for at least seven years, dating back to the middle school years. That and those 15 starts last season means that Watson’s integration as a full-time starter should not have too many hiccups. Watson is part of the junior class that includes Jaloni Cambridge and Elsa Lemmilä, so nobody who will get starting minutes can claim their teammates are a stranger. As is the case with every shooter, there will be hot and cold spells for Watson. The games to pay close attention to for the guard are the ones that follow a cold shooting day. Past shooting guards who excelled in McGuff’s system, Gray and Taylor Mikesell, both knew that if they underperformed that it would not stop them shooting in the next game. Watson’s focus on building confidence will come in handy in those moments as Watson adjusts to being the primary No. 2 guard for the Scarlet and Gray. Highlights In this clip, Watson is in the point guard role and shows her connection with her teammates, ability to read space and speed with the ball. This kind of play from a shooting guard can open Ohio State up and give teammates more space to work on offense.

item.title: ‘Sometimes, you need a change’: Rival scouts, execs have thoughts on Yankees’ Aaron Boone decision
item.description: The Yankees have considered changing managers since being swept out of the postseason by the World Series-bound Rays two weeks ago. How could they not? Managing general partner Hal Steinbrenner and general manager Brian Cashman couldn’t ignore all those former Yankees calling out the organization for bad clubhouse culture. Those big names included Derek Jeter, Alex Rodriguez, CC Sabathia, Paul O’Neill, Joe Girardi and Anthony Rizzo. As NJ.com has been predicting , the Yankees will be sticking with Aaron Boone , although Monday night’s reports were slightly premature. NJ.com baseball columnist Bob Klapisch reported Tuesday that a final decision will be made soon for Boone to manage the final year of his contract, which will be his 10 th since succeeding Girardi. Klapisch also reported that this is Steinbrenner’s call and the upcoming work stoppage has played a role in the decision to retain Boone. If the Yankees fired Boone now and found a replacement in a few weeks, the new manager wouldn’t be permitted to talk to his players from the time the lockout begins on Dec. 1 until it ends. The offseason is a critical bonding period for new managers and players. If this lockout lasts until summer, as many predict, spring training could be shortened to three weeks instead of six, similar to 2020 when COVID shortened the season to 60 games. Boone’s time with the Yankees is checkered. He has a great regular-season résumé — nine consecutive winning seasons, eight postseasons, one pennant and a .583 winning percentage that is second among active managers and 17 th best all-time. But Boone hasn’t won a World Series, and it’s now been 17 years since the Yankees’ last championship in 2009. Also, clubhouse culture criticism reflects poorly on any skipper. Are Jazz Chisholm’s antics on Boone? Does Cashman deserve blame for trading for a player who was a problem with the Marlins? Are the Yankees making the right move in keeping Boone? NJ.com sought opinions from four people in baseball who follow the Yankees closely. All four were granted anonymity because they’re not authorized by their organizations to publicly comment on opposing teams. Here’s their take: NATIONAL LEAGUE SCOUT “I like Aaron Boone. I think that his inability to have the courage to sit Jazz Chisholm when he needed to sit became a problem. I saw Joe Torre lose the clubhouse when he was in New York, Charlie Manuel lose the clubhouse when he was in Philly. I saw Terry Francona lose the clubhouse when he was in Boston. I’m seeing the same thing with Aaron. That doesn’t make them bad managers, but sometimes, you need a change. Sometimes you need somebody that’s not so nice to the players. “When you watch the Yankees, you see all the lackadaisical crap, the bonehead defensive plays, the bonehead baserunning, the Jazz Chisholm show. item.content:encoded: The Yankees have considered changing managers since being swept out of the postseason by the World Series-bound Rays two weeks ago. How could they not? Managing general partner Hal Steinbrenner and general manager Brian Cashman couldn’t ignore all those former Yankees calling out the organization for bad clubhouse culture. Those big names included Derek Jeter, Alex Rodriguez, CC Sabathia, Paul O’Neill, Joe Girardi and Anthony Rizzo. As NJ.com has been predicting , the Yankees will be sticking with Aaron Boone , although Monday night’s reports were slightly premature. NJ.com baseball columnist Bob Klapisch reported Tuesday that a final decision will be made soon for Boone to manage the final year of his contract, which will be his 10 th since succeeding Girardi. Klapisch also reported that this is Steinbrenner’s call and the upcoming work stoppage has played a role in the decision to retain Boone. If the Yankees fired Boone now and found a replacement in a few weeks, the new manager wouldn’t be permitted to talk to his players from the time the lockout begins on Dec. 1 until it ends. The offseason is a critical bonding period for new managers and players. If this lockout lasts until summer, as many predict, spring training could be shortened to three weeks instead of six, similar to 2020 when COVID shortened the season to 60 games. Boone’s time with the Yankees is checkered. He has a great regular-season résumé — nine consecutive winning seasons, eight postseasons, one pennant and a .583 winning percentage that is second among active managers and 17 th best all-time. But Boone hasn’t won a World Series, and it’s now been 17 years since the Yankees’ last championship in 2009. Also, clubhouse culture criticism reflects poorly on any skipper. Are Jazz Chisholm’s antics on Boone? Does Cashman deserve blame for trading for a player who was a problem with the Marlins? Are the Yankees making the right move in keeping Boone? NJ.com sought opinions from four people in baseball who follow the Yankees closely. All four were granted anonymity because they’re not authorized by their organizations to publicly comment on opposing teams. Here’s their take: NATIONAL LEAGUE SCOUT “I like Aaron Boone. I think that his inability to have the courage to sit Jazz Chisholm when he needed to sit became a problem. I saw Joe Torre lose the clubhouse when he was in New York, Charlie Manuel lose the clubhouse when he was in Philly. I saw Terry Francona lose the clubhouse when he was in Boston. I’m seeing the same thing with Aaron. That doesn’t make them bad managers, but sometimes, you need a change. Sometimes you need somebody that’s not so nice to the players. “When you watch the Yankees, you see all the lackadaisical crap, the bonehead defensive plays, the bonehead baserunning, the Jazz Chisholm show. That’s sadly a young, five-tool player who hurts you more than he’ll ever help you. “I would have made a change. I think Aaron’s a good manager. He’s a good person. He sticks up for his players. He takes the slings for some of the crap his players do, but at a certain point, you can’t just continue to be their friend. “Pat Murphy just took the Brewers to the World Series. He benches guys, but you never hear anyone say, “I wouldn’t want to play for Murphy.’ His guys love him because it’s consistent. If Aaron Judge pissed Pat Murphy off, Pat Murphy would call out Aaron Judge. I don’t think Aaron Boone would do that. Even when Murphy was the Brewers’ bench guy, if guys were screwing around during a spring training practice, he’d air them out in front of whoever was there. I don’t think Aaron Boone would ever do that. “Yeah, I think the Yankees need a change. There are good managers out there who would air guys out. Buck Showalter isn’t young, but he wouldn’t be a bad choice. Brandon Hyde wouldn’t be a bad choice.” AMERICAN LEAGUE SCOUT 1 “You know what? That’s a tough one. I’d keep Boone there. I like what he’s done. It ain’t his fault that a pitcher can’t win a big game. It’s not his fault that Aaron Judge gets hurt. It’s not his fault that Giancarlo Stanton is overpaid and can’t stay on the field. And it’s not Boone’s fault that Cashman doesn’t move some of those minor leaguers or players to go out get pieces to help them win. That’s why Judge is chirping now. “The stuff that Jazz is getting away with, that is on Boone, and that’s when he needs to clamp down. I know it’s New York, and I know Boone would get hollered at by management for being too tough, but at some point, you’ve got to sit Jazz down for a week and prove a point. Sometimes you have to do that. Sometimes you’ve got to call a guy out like that. Then you go to the people above you and say, ‘Look, if you want to win and you want to get the best of this guy, you got to call him out.’ Jazz knows he can get away with it and he knows Boone ain’t gonna call him out, so nothing’s gonna be done, and I think that’s total BS. “Here’s another thing: Teams used to be afraid of the Yankees. Not anymore. They’re on even ground now. Baltimore is not afraid of them anymore. Toronto’s not afraid of them anymore. Tampa definitely’s not afraid of them. The Yankees have more stars and a bigger payroll, but other teams now say, ‘Be patient, boys, something stupid is going to happen. Let’s wait to see what Jazz does.’ That’s on the whole organization. That’s on Boone. That’s on Cashman. That’s on Steinbrenner. Yeah.” NATIONAL LEAGUE EXECUTIVE “I guess the first thing is, who are you going to go get to replace Boone if the Yankees fired him? You’ve got teams out there right now that can’t find a manager. Look at some of the teams that hired guys in the last year. Who’s better than Boone? Now I’m not saying Boone’s the greatest, but who do you want to put on the list? That would be my question to all the people that want to replace him. “I think it’s going to be a short year next year. It’s the last year of Boone’s contract. Give him one more shot. Get everybody healthy. If everybody was healthy this year, they might win the division. You never know. “The bottom line, I don’t think the Yankees are outmanaged. At the end of the day, these guys have to hit the ball, play the game, field the ball. Right? They obviously pitched well. It again came down to the playoffs where they were a couple hits away here and there. I didn’t see a team that was outmanaged, but the culture is definitely something that you could address as being a real thing. “Culture is a very big deal. I would say that there were some issues this year. Obviously, you see a guy with a sucker in his mouth out in the field. That’s a problem. But I don’t know if it was just Jazz. “I don’t know that the culture was bad. It might be a little stale at some point. On every team, eventually things run stale. Was Dusty Baker a bad manager? He moved around four or five times to different teams and the guy should be or will be a Hall of Fame manager. He was great for culture. “I wonder if Boone has anyone policing the clubhouse. In Boston, the Red Sox always had Dustin Pedroia and David Ortiz to police Manny Ramirez. Was anyone there to do that on the Yankees this year? Judge was hurt half the year and not on every roadtrip. Giancarlo Stanton wasn’t around almost the whole year. I don’t know. “Again, when I watched the Yankees, I didn’t see a team that was getting outmanaged and I’ll come back to who are you getting that’s better than Boone? I can’t think of anyone.” AMERICAN LEAGUE SCOUT 2 “I don’t think Boone’s the problem. I don’t think Boone’s ever been allowed to manage. I think Boone’s given a script, and he follows the script. There’s a reason why Joe Girardi was let go. He didn’t follow the script. It’s a symptom of Major League Baseball now. Stuff comes down from the front office, the manager is giving a script and he runs with it. When Cashman says Boone is making the lineup, I have zero belief in that. Zero. “I think Boone’s biggest flaw is he has

item.title: Looking at 2026 season report card for Padres players
item.description: SAN DIEGO, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 07: Jason Adam #40 of the San Diego Padres delivers the pitch against the Milwaukee Brewers during the sixth inning in game four of the National League Division Series at Petco Park on October 07, 2026 in San Diego, California. (Photo by Orlando Ramirez/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Tampa Bay Rays punched their ticket to the 2026 World Series to take on the Milwaukee Brewers with a win over the Cleveland Guardians in Tampa Bay on Monday night. At best, there are seven games left in the MLB season so Lincoln Zdunich of Gaslamp Ball thought it was a good time to look back at the season for the San Diego Padres — more specifically, he takes a look at the individual players and gives them a grade for their performance. Zdunich started with reliever Jason Adam who suffered a quadriceps injury that cut his 2025 season short and he spent significant time on the injured list this season as well. It is unfortunate timing for the right-hander as he is set to be a free agent at the conclusion of the World Series. The injuries and the concerns that will surely be discussed about further injuries will dampen his earnings on the open market, but he has shown that he can be dominant when healthy. The question facing the Padres and their fans is, “Should Adam be re-signed?” That question may not be able to be answered until the San Diego executives determine if they are going to try to re-sign Adrian Morejon or if Yuki Matsui is going to exercise his player option and opt-out of his current contract. Left-handed relievers are commonly more highly sought after than right-handers. If Padres president of baseball operations A.J. Preller wants to commit to re-signing Morejon that could impact an offer to Adam. If Matsui opts-out and Preller does not try to re-sign him that could unlock additional money to offer Adam. The thing Preller and his staff have to figure out is will Adam stay healthy and if he does, will he return to the 2024 pitcher who served as part of a dominant backend trio for San Diego with Tanner Scott and Robert Suarez. Preller could stick to his oft-used tactics of signing Adam to a “prove-it deal.” Adam would have the opportunity to show he can stay healthy and perform and he could also have options from the player and team side that would give him some security and flexibility. At the end of it all, Adam is a good major league pitcher. More than that, he seems to be a good human who is genuinely loved and appreciated by his teammates. That being said, it all comes down to numbers. Adam played 2026 on a one-year, $6.675 million deal. It would be hard to go much beyond that given his recent injuries but if he would consider a similar one year deal or a multi-year deal that has a similar cost per year he could be back in the Padres bullpen in 2027. Do you, the Friar Faithful, think Adam should be re-signed? Padres News: Padres outfield prospect Alex McCoy is making noise and making a name for himself in Arizona Fa

Baseball News: Aaron Boone will return as New York Yankees manager for final year of his deal in 2027. The New York Mets traded for and traded away Freddy Peralta and will now watch him in the World Series. The Los Angeles Dodgers will have to learn from 2026 season and decide how best to help Shohei Ohtani stay healthy in 2027. Teruaki Sato of the Hanshin Tigers in the Nippon Professional Baseball will be posted for MLB teams . The Athletics announced the hiring of Taylor Smith as their president of baseball operations. The Detroit Tigers will have a decision to make about Kenley Jansen this offseason.

item.title: Just in: Barcelona midfield mainstay set to be rested against PSG – report
item.description: Just in: Barcelona midfield mainstay set to be rested against PSG – report Barcelona are reportedly preparing to rest Rodri for their Champions League meeting with Paris Saint-Germain , with Hansi Flick weighing the midfielder’s workload ahead of this weekend’s El Clasico against Real Madrid. According to journalist Alfredo Martinez , the Spanish international is expected to sit out the PSG clash despite having no injury or physical problems. Notably, the potential decision would be a result of a workload management measure rather than a response to a fitness concern, with Barcelona facing another major test just days later. Flick faces difficult Rodri decision before PSG clash Resting one of Barcelona’s most influential midfielders against PSG would be a significant call, particularly given the quality of the opposition. However, Rodri’s growing importance to Flick’s side makes managing his minutes increasingly relevant as the season progresses. The midfielder endured a slow start to his Barcelona career because of back problems and a registration delay, but his situation changed once he became established in the starting XI. Rodri could be rested against PSG. (Photo by Fran Santiago/Getty Images) Flick subsequently had little reason to leave him out, given the Spaniard’s influence in the middle of the pitch. So far this season, Rodri has played 690 minutes across 10 matches in all competitions, starting eight of them. That works out at an average of 69 minutes per appearance, showing how regularly he has featured since becoming part of the team’s plans. Although the PSG fixture would ordinarily be an occasion to field the strongest possible midfield, Barcelona must also consider the demands of their upcoming meeting with Real Madrid. El Clasico could influence Barcelona’s midfield selection The prospect of El Clasico gives Flick an additional reason to consider rotation. Keeping Rodri fresh for the weekend could prove valuable, particularly with Barcelona facing a demanding schedule and little margin for error in major fixtures. Rodri averages almost 70 minutes per match for Barcelona. (Photo by Fran Santiago/Getty Images) The challenge is that replacing Rodri means losing a particular blend of control, experience and tactical influence. This is because none of Barcelona’s alternative midfielders necessarily offers an identical profile, leaving Flick to decide whether the benefits of resting his key player outweigh the potential cost against PSG. Gavi, Bernal and Olmo offer Flick alternatives If Rodri is left out, Flick still has several options to partner Pedri in central midfield, with Gavi, Marc Bernal, Fermin Lopez and Dani Olmo among the candidates who could be given greater responsibility against PSG. Each would bring different qualities to the role, giving Flick flexibility in how he approaches the contest, although none would replicate the exact profile of Rodri. item.title: Chivu: "We have to be ourselves: we want to win tomorrow"
item.description: Chivu: "We have to be ourselves: we want to win tomorrow" The eve of Inter vs. Shakhtar Donetsk, Matchday 3 of the 2026/27 UEFA Champions League League Phase. Ahead of the clash with the Ukrainian side, Nerazzurri Head Coach Cristian Chivu , joined by Alessandro Bastoni , will take questions from the media in a press conference live from the Inter Training Center: Do you think it is right to combine last season’s defeats with this season’s Champions League losses? “I’ve never counted them myself, but if the figures are brought to my attention, I have to respond. There’s no need to keep reminding us of it. We’ve lost two matches this season and we need to rediscover our energy and the right feelings, which go hand in hand with our ambitions. We must focus on what needs to be done tomorrow and be ready in every respect: mentally, physically and tactically.” What happened at half-time in Bologna? “I speak quietly, raise my voice, laugh and joke, but I do the same things I do at home with my children. The love I feel for my players is very close to the love I feel for my family. That doesn’t change, whether I speak quietly or get angry.” How can you turn difficult starts to matches into a different attitude? “I’m pleased when a player takes responsibility, but I’m the one primarily responsible. Perhaps I’m not managing to communicate what’s needed. It works both ways; it’s not an issue that concerns only them. If we had an important season last year, it was because every member of the group took responsibility.” What kind of match do you expect? “Shakhtar are a strong team. They play in the Champions League, and every team in this competition is tactically developed and has quality, experience, technically gifted players, pace and intensity, as well as a coach who sets them up well. They bring plenty of intensity, both on and off the ball. We have to be ourselves, with confidence in what we’ve earned over time, while also recognising that what we’ve done in the past counts for less. What matters is today, as we prepare for tomorrow.” Has someone from this team putting themselves forward as a Champions League contender caused damage? Why did it happen? “I answered this a few weeks ago, saying that when questions are asked, we respond out of politeness and duty. We’ve never said that we have to win it; we’ve said that it’s a dream. Right now, after two defeats, we must think only about tomorrow. The priority is to win a match first and foremost, and that means tomorrow’s game.” What do you think needs to change? “I was talking about myself and what I can do better to communicate certain things and remove others: bring more attention, more concern and more motivation, and see whether I can be more involved in preparing for a match and reading it as it unfolds. item.content:encoded: Chivu: "We have to be ourselves: we want to win tomorrow" The eve of Inter vs. Shakhtar Donetsk, Matchday 3 of the 2026/27 UEFA Champions League League Phase. Ahead of the clash with the Ukrainian side, Nerazzurri Head Coach Cristian Chivu , joined by Alessandro Bastoni , will take questions from the media in a press conference live from the Inter Training Center: Do you think it is right to combine last season’s defeats with this season’s Champions League losses? “I’ve never counted them myself, but if the figures are brought to my attention, I have to respond. There’s no need to keep reminding us of it. We’ve lost two matches this season and we need to rediscover our energy and the right feelings, which go hand in hand with our ambitions. We must focus on what needs to be done tomorrow and be ready in every respect: mentally, physically and tactically.” What happened at half-time in Bologna? “I speak quietly, raise my voice, laugh and joke, but I do the same things I do at home with my children. The love I feel for my players is very close to the love I feel for my family. That doesn’t change, whether I speak quietly or get angry.” How can you turn difficult starts to matches into a different attitude? “I’m pleased when a player takes responsibility, but I’m the one primarily responsible. Perhaps I’m not managing to communicate what’s needed. It works both ways; it’s not an issue that concerns only them. If we had an important season last year, it was because every member of the group took responsibility.” What kind of match do you expect? “Shakhtar are a strong team. They play in the Champions League, and every team in this competition is tactically developed and has quality, experience, technically gifted players, pace and intensity, as well as a coach who sets them up well. They bring plenty of intensity, both on and off the ball. We have to be ourselves, with confidence in what we’ve earned over time, while also recognising that what we’ve done in the past counts for less. What matters is today, as we prepare for tomorrow.” Has someone from this team putting themselves forward as a Champions League contender caused damage? Why did it happen? “I answered this a few weeks ago, saying that when questions are asked, we respond out of politeness and duty. We’ve never said that we have to win it; we’ve said that it’s a dream. Right now, after two defeats, we must think only about tomorrow. The priority is to win a match first and foremost, and that means tomorrow’s game.” What do you think needs to change? “I was talking about myself and what I can do better to communicate certain things and remove others: bring more attention, more concern and more motivation, and see whether I can be more involved in preparing for a match and reading it as it unfolds. I never point the finger at my players. I take responsibility for what happens on the pitch, especially the negative aspects and individual mistakes. I’m their coach, and it’s important to understand that this group has been playing under pressure for several years. That’s a credit to them, because they’ve earned that reputation from the outside. They’ve been competitive for seven years. It’s my job to take responsibility for certain things. I understand what they’re experiencing, and the coach has to be the main person held accountable. I’m the one who needs to improve first.” How can a coach change a team’s attitude at half-time? “I don’t know. What are we talking about? If we start badly, is it my fault, but if we change the outcome at half-time, is it down to me? It’s a combination of things. You understand certain aspects of the game and react to the opposition while maintaining your own identity, which is also something we’re trying to add to this team. Half-time helps us understand how the match is unfolding, but the players deserve credit for reacting and adapting to the opposition, their qualities and their ability. We don’t play alone; we play against tactically developed teams who give everything against us because everyone wants to beat us. It’s been that way for seven years. A match presents different challenges, even when things go against you. What matters is how you react and understand the difficulties, so that you can find the balance and maturity needed to get the result.” Do you think comebacks after going behind are more about mentality or balance on the pitch? “I don’t think I’m arrogant. We talk too much about nothing and are always looking for the negatives. I’m an optimist by nature, because that’s how I’m made. I look at the positives and at how we respond to conceding goals. I need to analyse in depth why it happens, but I don’t want to discuss it. I’m responsible for everything that doesn’t work; the credit belongs to the players and their maturity, because they understand how to react and what they need to do during a match. The ideal situation is not to concede, but we’re not perfect, either as a team or as individuals. There are things that affect the course of a match, but what matters to me is that the group does everything it can to get the result. I don’t want defeats to become tragedies, because they aren’t and they won’t be. I have the feeling that we’re expected to meet certain obligations while others aren’t, and that isn’t right. I have to reassure the players, and they do their best. After that, we can win, lose or draw.”

item.title: NFC West Recap: 49ers continue to distance themselves; Rams and Seahawks lose
item.description: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 19: Head Coach Kyle Shanahan of the San Francisco 49ers walks the field after winning the game against the Washington Commanders at Levi's Stadium on October 19, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers had another good week of football. Sure, their 23-17 win over the Washington Commanders unnecessarily came down to the wire, but they still won. The best part is, everyone else lost! AGAIN! The 49ers have beaten the Commanders—a team the Seattle Seahawks lost to. They have also beaten the Denver Broncos, a team both the Rams and Seahawks lost to. Should tiebreakers come into play, those two victories could be a deciding factor. So that puts the 49ers at 6-0 and 3-0 in the division. With the losses, they now have a three-game lead (and change if you could tiebreakers) over the second-place Seahawks. Yes, the Commanders win wasn’t pretty, but the 49ers are 6-0, and if we have to endure a game like that Commanders game to be 6-0, I don’t think there’s a fan in the world who wouldn’t take that. It’s not without some wrinkles. Wide receiver Mike Evans may miss some time . While Christian Kirk has resumed practice, it might take some time to get in sync with Brock Purdy. At least the 49ers get Dre Greenlaw back next week and maybe Nick Bosa. Seattle Seahawks (3-3) The biggest thing about the Seahawks’ loss to the Denver Broncos isn’t that they lost a game they probably should have won; it’s that Bo Nix may be getting more criticism for his play than Sam Darnold. Ryan Fitzpatrick absolutely destroyed Bo Nix on live TV 💀 pic.twitter.com/HGu3T5fi4A — PredictArena (@PredictArena) October 16, 2026 And he should. Nix has had a tendency to come back in the second half in 2026, but he didn’t do any of that here. You can also add in some very bad decision-making. Nix went 17 for 27 and 107 yards passing. Yes, 107 yards passing and the Broncos won. It’s fair to note the Broncos also had 74 yards rushing. So how did the Broncos win? Defense, all defense. How did the Seahawks lose? Well, not being able to run the ball might be the biggest reason. 113 yards total. Rashid Shaheed losing one of his two fumbles doesn’t help. Then there’s the other quarterback. Sam Darnold had two interceptions, zero touchdowns, and five sacks. 17-14, Broncos. The Broncos are 4-2 after that stat line from Bo Nix. He didn’t throw a touchdown or an interception and got sacked twice compared to Darnold’s five. Do the Broncos look like a 4-2 team? That’s up to you. The Seahawks are now games (yes, plural) behind the 49ers, and it’s not going to get any easier. Arizona Cardinals (2-4)/Los Angeles Rams (2-4) Oh, you know what time it is. Let’s Ram It! item.content:encoded: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 19: Head Coach Kyle Shanahan of the San Francisco 49ers walks the field after winning the game against the Washington Commanders at Levi's Stadium on October 19, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers had another good week of football. Sure, their 23-17 win over the Washington Commanders unnecessarily came down to the wire, but they still won. The best part is, everyone else lost! AGAIN! The 49ers have beaten the Commanders—a team the Seattle Seahawks lost to. They have also beaten the Denver Broncos, a team both the Rams and Seahawks lost to. Should tiebreakers come into play, those two victories could be a deciding factor. So that puts the 49ers at 6-0 and 3-0 in the division. With the losses, they now have a three-game lead (and change if you could tiebreakers) over the second-place Seahawks. Yes, the Commanders win wasn’t pretty, but the 49ers are 6-0, and if we have to endure a game like that Commanders game to be 6-0, I don’t think there’s a fan in the world who wouldn’t take that. It’s not without some wrinkles. Wide receiver Mike Evans may miss some time . While Christian Kirk has resumed practice, it might take some time to get in sync with Brock Purdy. At least the 49ers get Dre Greenlaw back next week and maybe Nick Bosa. Seattle Seahawks (3-3) The biggest thing about the Seahawks’ loss to the Denver Broncos isn’t that they lost a game they probably should have won; it’s that Bo Nix may be getting more criticism for his play than Sam Darnold. Ryan Fitzpatrick absolutely destroyed Bo Nix on live TV 💀 pic.twitter.com/HGu3T5fi4A — PredictArena (@PredictArena) October 16, 2026 And he should. Nix has had a tendency to come back in the second half in 2026, but he didn’t do any of that here. You can also add in some very bad decision-making. Nix went 17 for 27 and 107 yards passing. Yes, 107 yards passing and the Broncos won. It’s fair to note the Broncos also had 74 yards rushing. So how did the Broncos win? Defense, all defense. How did the Seahawks lose? Well, not being able to run the ball might be the biggest reason. 113 yards total. Rashid Shaheed losing one of his two fumbles doesn’t help. Then there’s the other quarterback. Sam Darnold had two interceptions, zero touchdowns, and five sacks. 17-14, Broncos. The Broncos are 4-2 after that stat line from Bo Nix. He didn’t throw a touchdown or an interception and got sacked twice compared to Darnold’s five. Do the Broncos look like a 4-2 team? That’s up to you. The Seahawks are now games (yes, plural) behind the 49ers, and it’s not going to get any easier. Arizona Cardinals (2-4)/Los Angeles Rams (2-4) Oh, you know what time it is. Let’s Ram It! Let’s Ram it all the way to last place in the NFC West. The Arizona Cardinals not only beat the Los Angeles Rams, but did so by field-goal-ing the Rams to death. Six field goals were all the Cardinals needed to get the 18-16 victory. This was a Los Angeles Rams team that some thought would go undefeated before the season began. Now they are last place in their own division. My, what a tangled web we weave. And the Rams had a chance to win this thing. They marched down the field, got the touchdown, and the Cardinals only had 45 seconds left with no timeouts. Turns out 45 seconds is too much time for Jacoby Brissett, because next thing you know he’s pushing the ball down the field and getting into field goal range in 10 of those 45 seconds. Many are saying the Rams get an easier schedule so they can right the ship, but again: They lost to a team via six field goals. The only other team the Cardinals have beaten is from Los Angeles, and that team, the Chargers, is 0-6 right now. And yes, the Rams lost their kicker early in the game and didn’t have a kicker to make field goals. Then again, should the Rams need a kicker for the Cardinals? That’s a huge win for the Cardinals and an equally miserable loss for the Rams. Are they out? No. But they are now in last place with several divisional losses on them as well. They are almost at “run the table to get in the playoffs” territory. Almost. And it gets worse. First, wide receiver Davante Adams is out 6-10 weeks due to a hamstring injury. That’s devastating for the wide receiver group (something 49ers fans know all too well). Second, their shiny new kicker, Blake Grupe, was injured on Sunday, which was enough to add him to injured reserve. So the Rams need to overcome a four-game deficit without a kicker or their veteran wide receiver. Onto Week 7 The 49ers will travel to face the Atlanta Falcons, a game with the dreaded 10:00 AM start time. Not exactly ideal when the Falcons have been humming for a couple of games until Sunday—when the Chicago Bears crushed them. That score says 31-23, but 16 of the Falcons’ 23 points came in the fourth quarter. Meanwhile, Chicago was scoring touchdowns until the fourth quarter. Regardless of Atlanta’s performance, they have the best running back in the game in Bijan Robinson. With Robinson, the Falcons can run the ball, and if you’ve watched them lately, he’s not exactly the easiest thing to stop. It’s a great test for the 49ers, who have limited explosive runs. The Seahawks host the Kansas City Chiefs as the Sunday Night Football game. It feels strange to want the Seahawks to win just to hand the Chiefs a loss, but the Chiefs could do the 49ers a favor by putting the Seahawks to 3-4. As much as some of us may dislike both teams, that will be a fun game to watch. Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III will probably be the star of the show; the Seahawks running game hasn’t been the same since he left in free agency, and the Chiefs have had a running game since acquiring him. The Cardinals host the Denver Broncos. The same Denver Broncos who managed to beat the Seahawks. Given what we’ve seen of this Cardinals team, a win isn’t out of the ordinary. The Rams will have their second straight week of not playing on primetime. They might play a bit more on Sunday afternoon if the league flexes them out of anything in the future. They host the Las Vegas Raiders. The Raiders lost to the Buffalo Bills, but were in it until the end. The Rams could be their get-right game. 1st: San Francisco 49ers Next at Atlanta Falcons 2nd: Seattle Seahawks; Next: vs. Kansas City Chiefs (Sunday Night Football ) 3rd: Arizona Cardinals; Next: vs. Denver Broncos 4th: Los Angeles Rams; Next: at Las Vegas Raiders

item.title: Tom Brady faces criticism over Sam Darnold ‘acting’ remark
item.description: Source: OSCAR GONZALEZ FUENTES/Shutterstock.com Tom Brady drew criticism after questioning Sam Darnold’s reaction to a late hit during the Seattle Seahawks’ 32-29 loss to the San Francisco 49ers on Oct. 11. The former quarterback’s broadcast comments quickly became a talking point beyond the game itself. The controversy began when San Francisco linebacker Dre Greenlaw made contact with Darnold near the sideline after the Seattle quarterback had run out of bounds. Officials penalized Greenlaw for unnecessary roughness, but Brady disagreed with the decision and suggested Darnold exaggerated the contact. Brady’s remark, “Darnold with the acting,” prompted criticism from viewers who felt the veteran analyst was dismissing a legitimate concern about quarterback safety. The incident also reopened discussion about how Brady evaluates players now that he has moved from the field to the broadcast booth. Brady’s comment sparks a debate The incident occurred during the second quarter of a closely contested divisional matchup. Darnold had scrambled toward the sideline when Greenlaw continued his pursuit and made contact after the quarterback had moved out of bounds. Brady questioned whether the hit warranted a penalty, arguing during the broadcast that Greenlaw was attempting to prevent Darnold from gaining additional yards. He characterized the contact as a minor nudge and criticized the quarterback’s reaction. That assessment became the central issue for viewers who believed the contact deserved closer scrutiny. While analysts regularly disagree about officiating, Brady’s wording made the discussion more personal by appearing to question Darnold’s sincerity rather than focusing solely on the rule. Why fans questioned Brady’s judgment Criticism centered partly on Brady’s own experience as a quarterback. During his playing career, he benefited from rules designed to protect passers from dangerous contact, making his dismissal of Darnold’s reaction seem contradictory to some viewers. Social media users questioned whether Brady would have reacted differently if a defender had made similar contact with him. Others argued that the analyst was being unnecessarily harsh toward Darnold during a game in which Seattle was already under pressure. The criticism represented a range of fan opinions rather than a universal response. Some viewers agreed with Brady’s interpretation of the play, while others believed the officials had correctly recognized contact that occurred after Darnold reached the sideline. Greenlaw’s hit escalates into a sideline confrontation The play became more serious when the confrontation continued near Seattle’s sideline. Greenlaw headbutted Seahawks linebacker Ernest Jones IV, who was not wearing his helmet, prompting officials to eject the San Francisco defender. The NFL later suspended Greenlaw for one game, and his appeal was denied. The league’s disciplinary action followed the headbutt, which was separate from the unnecessary roughness pen

He characterized the contact as a minor nudge and criticized the quarterback’s reaction. That assessment became the central issue for viewers who believed the contact deserved closer scrutiny. While analysts regularly disagree about officiating, Brady’s wording made the discussion more personal by appearing to question Darnold’s sincerity rather than focusing solely on the rule. Why fans questioned Brady’s judgment Criticism centered partly on Brady’s own experience as a quarterback. During his playing career, he benefited from rules designed to protect passers from dangerous contact, making his dismissal of Darnold’s reaction seem contradictory to some viewers. Social media users questioned whether Brady would have reacted differently if a defender had made similar contact with him. Others argued that the analyst was being unnecessarily harsh toward Darnold during a game in which Seattle was already under pressure. The criticism represented a range of fan opinions rather than a universal response. Some viewers agreed with Brady’s interpretation of the play, while others believed the officials had correctly recognized contact that occurred after Darnold reached the sideline. Greenlaw’s hit escalates into a sideline confrontation The play became more serious when the confrontation continued near Seattle’s sideline. Greenlaw headbutted Seahawks linebacker Ernest Jones IV, who was not wearing his helmet, prompting officials to eject the San Francisco defender. The NFL later suspended Greenlaw for one game, and his appeal was denied. The league’s disciplinary action followed the headbutt, which was separate from the unnecessary roughness penalty assessed for the contact with Darnold. The sequence complicated the discussion surrounding Brady’s remarks. Although the analyst had questioned the original penalty, the confrontation that followed demonstrated how quickly an on-field disagreement can escalate when players lose their composure. Source: operations@newsimages.co.uk/Depositphotos Darnold’s performance adds context to the criticism Darnold finished the game against San Francisco with 195 passing yards, 1 touchdown and 2 interceptions. He was also sacked 5 times as the Seahawks fell short in a game decided by 3 points. Seattle’s offensive struggles gave Brady plenty to discuss during the broadcast. However, critics argued that questioning the quarterback’s reaction to a late hit was different from analyzing his decisions, passing accuracy or ability to handle pressure. The loss dropped Seattle to 3-2 at the time, leaving the team looking for greater consistency. Darnold had helped lead the Seahawks to a strong previous season, but his early 2026 performances included turnovers that became an increasing concern. Brady’s transition from quarterback to analyst Brady has spent decades in the public eye as one of football’s most accomplished players. His transition to television commentary has placed him in a different role, requiring him to assess decisions and performances rather than make them himself. As Fox Sports’ lead NFL analyst, Brady brings firsthand knowledge of quarterback play and defensive strategy. That experience can provide valuable insight, but it also means his opinions receive close attention from viewers familiar with his playing career. The Darnold controversy illustrates the challenge of balancing direct analysis with measured language. A strong opinion can make a broadcast more engaging, but viewers may push back when commentary appears to judge a player’s motives rather than the observable play. The debate over player protection continues NFL rules prohibit forcibly contacting a runner who is out of bounds. Defenders must make an effort to avoid contact and are responsible for recognizing when a runner has crossed the boundary, subject to the rule’s exception for doubtful cases. These protections apply to all runners, including quarterbacks. Officials must assess the timing and nature of the contact. A defender’s pursuit of a runner does not automatically make an out-of-bounds hit legal. Brady disagreed with the unnecessary-roughness penalty against Greenlaw, arguing that the contact was minor. Officials nevertheless assessed the penalty, leaving viewers debating their interpretation of the play. Source: operations@newsimages.co.uk/Depositphotos Brady’s reputation shapes the reaction Brady’s 7 Super Bowl victories and long career with the New England Patriots and Tampa Bay Buccaneers established him as one of football’s most recognizable figures. That history also shapes how viewers interpret his commentary. His experience brings a former quarterback’s perspective to the broadcast booth, where even a brief remark can attract considerable attention. Fun fact: Brady was 4 years old when he attended the NFC Championship Game on January 10, 1982, and witnessed Dwight Clark’s famous play known as “The Catch.” What the controversy means for Brady and Darnold The backlash is unlikely to settle the debate over the hit, but it highlights how closely viewers scrutinize high-profile commentators. Brady’s words became part of the story because fans expected him to understand the risks quarterbacks face when defenders make late contact. For Darnold, the incident added another layer to a difficult stretch of the season. Seattle still needed to address offensive turnovers and protection problems, issues that would have mattered regardless of the broadcast discussion. For Brady, the episode serves as a reminder that credibility in sports broadcasting depends not only on football knowledge but also on how analysis is delivered. His assessment generated discussion, yet the disagreement over the play remains a matter of interpretation among viewers. TL;DR Tom Brady questioned Sam Darnold’s reaction to an out-of-bounds hit during Seattle’s 32–29 loss to San Francisco on October 11, 2026. Officials penalized Dre Greenlaw for unnecessary roughness. Greenlaw was subsequently ejected for headbutting Ernest Jones IV and received a 1-game suspension, which was upheld on appeal. Brady’s comments drew criticism, while some viewers agreed with his interpretation. Darnold finished with 195 passing yards, 1 touchdown and 2 interceptions. item.title: Big Ten Football Power Poll: Week Seven
item.description: BLOOMINGTON, INDIANA - OCTOBER 17: Jeremiah Smith #4 of the Ohio State Buckeyes celebrates a touchdown during the fourth quarter against the Indiana Hoosiers at Memorial Stadium on October 17, 2026 in Bloomington, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images Week Seven in the college football world was insane. Seven of the top ten teams in the country lost this week. Three different SEC teams lost to unranked opponents. But over here in the Big Ten—well chalk reigned supreme. Yes one of those top ten teams that lost was Indiana—but they lost to #4 Ohio State. And frankly, if their star receiver isn’t an idiot—they win. The rest of the conference matchups this week went about as you would expect. But there is plenty of drama brewing with injuries hitting some teams, and rivalry matchups a foot in the next few weeks that should have lots of implications on the conference pecking order going forward. #1 Ohio State Buckeyes 6-1 (1) Win 19-15 @ Indiana The Buckeyes took care of business….mostly against Indiana. It was a great back and forth battle, but once Buckeyes QB Julien Sayin went out with a shoulder injury, his backup true freshman Luke Fahey looked completely lost. He was not good ending the game 0-2 and running twice for -2 yards. The Buckeyes should have lost, but Nick Marsh lost where his feet where, and OSU skates through. They have a bye this week, but Fahey is going to need to get to speed fast as Sayin is reportedly out for several weeks. After the bye the Buckeyes to go USC, host Oregon and Northwestern, visits Lincoln and host Michigan. If Fahey can’t be a threat, there is no way the Buckeyes run that gauntlet undefeated. #2 Indiana Hoosiers 6-1 (2) Lose 19-15 vs Ohio State How close it was. If Marsh can just find his feet and stay inbounds, we are talking about Indiana as the dominant team in the conference. Now they fall behind the Buckeyes, but arguably have the better potential into the playoff. They go to Michigan this week at seven point favorites before hosting Minnesota, and then after a bye finish hosting USC, at Washington and hosting Purdue. The path for them to get back to the Big Ten Championship game likely goes through UCLA at this point, but if the Bruins stumble, Indiana will be relishing a rematch against the Buckeyes. #3 UCLA Bruins 6-0 (5) Win 17-7 vs Wisconsin It wasn’t pretty, and they definitely got some help from the refs, but the Bruins grinded out a 17-7 win to defeat Wisconsin and move to 6-0 on the season. Are the Bruins that good? I really don’t think they are, but they have beaten everyone in front of them. Luckily for them they don’t really have much in front of them the rest of the way either. They host Michigan State as a 14 point favorite this week, then host Nevada to complete their non-conference schedule. In November it’s a trip to Minnesota, hosting Illinois, heading to Ann Arbor and hosting USC. I’m not saying 12-0 is a great possibility, but its definitely not an unrealistic

In November it’s a trip to Minnesota, hosting Illinois, heading to Ann Arbor and hosting USC. I’m not saying 12-0 is a great possibility, but its definitely not an unrealistic one either. #4 USC Trojans 6-1 (3) BYE USC slips back one spot on their bye week thanks to their rivals win to remain undefeated. The Trojan offense continues to be great, but their defense is suspect at best. Did they figure some things out on their bye week? They head to Madison for a big Saturday night clash as three point favorites. Ohio State and Indiana loom next. There we really see just how good the Trojans are. #5 Iowa Hawkeyes 5-1 (4) BYE Iowa drops one spot as well thanks to the UCLA win. They come off of a bye and get to play back to back rivalry games as they head to Minneapolis to battle for Floyd of Rosedale this week, and then return home to host Wisconsin for that ugly cow trophy the following week. The schedule is fairly favorable in November for a run with home games against Purdue and Nebraska and trips to Northwestern and Illinois. #6 Oregon Ducks 4-2 (7) Win 17-14 vs Nebraska Oregon needs Dante Moore back in the worst way possible. After three quarters of awful QB play by their third string, they let Dylan Raiola come in against his former team. A week after absolutely stinking against UCLA Raiola came back and led the Ducks to a late win over Nebraska crushing the Husker spirits. They will now look to string a pair of wins together as they head to Illinois this week as 8.5 point favorites. #7 Northwestern Wildcats 6-1 (8) Win 24-21 @Michigan State Northwestern tried really hard to lose the Pat Fitzgerald bowl in East Lansing, but The Spartans just blew all opportunities late in the game and Northwestern didn’t kicking a field goal with two seconds left for the win. The Wildcats are now bowl eligible and with a few exceptions have a pretty favorable schedule left. That includes hosting Rutgers as 16.5 point favorites this weekend. Oregon, Iowa and Ohio State loom large the next three weeks after that, but the Wildcats are allready playing with house money. #8 Nebraska Cornhuskers 5-2 (6) Loss 17-14 @ Oregon Oh Nebraska. Same story different game. The Huskers had this game won, and then here comes their former QB to send them home unhappy. Now 0-33 against ranked teams in their last 33 games. The one score game record has got to be even worse. Just another Husker choke job. They get a bye this week to lick their wounds. #9 Michigan Wolverines (4-2) (12) Win 21-18 vs Penn State The Wolverines jump back up after a home win against Penn State. They finally benched their starting QB and went with Lloyd Carr’s grandson…which has seemed to work for Notre da…ooops. I don’t really know that Michigan is the 9th best team, but frankly at this point between 80-13 who can tell the damn difference. They are all beating up on one another in the mediocre middle. The Wolverines host Indiana as seven point underdogs this weekend, and frankly, I wouldn’t be shocked to see them lose by double that. #10 Wisconsin Badgers 4-2 (9) Loss 17-7 @ UCLA To say that the Badgers offense is putrid is putting it way too nicely. Colton Joseph is terrible throwing the ball. His 6-16 for 66 yard performance against the Bruins is embarrassing. But at least he ran for 71 yards on 18 carries. Yes the officiating was questionable at times, abd UCLA is good, but with that offense you won’t beat many teams. Except for maybe the one you play this week as USC comes to down with their awful defense. The Trojans are favored by 3, and the over/under is somehow 49.5? I don’t really see a 27-23 USC win here, but sure Vegas…you do you. #11 Minnesota Golden Gophers 4-2 (11) BYE Did Minnesota figure out how the hell to fix things during their bye week? PJ Fleck’s Monday press conference was not exactly encouraging. He know the pressure is on, and it’s Iowa week where Kirk Ferentz has been his daddy for almost every battle in the last 10 years. The line has gone from Iowa by 4 to Iowa by 7, so lots of betters think the Gophers won’t have the answers either on Homecoming. We will find out very soon #12 Washington Huskies 4-3 (13) Win 38-26 @ Purdue You never know what you might get in the Big Ten at night. The Huskies got beat by Minnesota, dropped a close one to USC, trounced by Iowa and then….dominates Purdue? Sure. Jedd Fisch went to the backup QB who was up and down, but up enough to get a must needed win. They now get a bye to rest of for a huge finish of the season. #13 Purdue Boilermakers 4-3 (10) Loss 38-26 vs Washington Well, Minnesota fans sure weren’t happy watching Purdue stink up the joint against Washington. Maybe it was just a perfect storm game, but the Boilers are definitely back on their heels a bit after that. They get a bye this week. #14 Illinois Fighting Illini 3-3 (14) BYE Illinois didn’t lose. But they didn’t win either. They come off of their bye to host Oregon as 8.5 point underdogs. Sees about right. #15 Rutgers Scarlet Knights 2-4 (17) Win 37-30 @ Maryland Rutgers find a way to get that second win by letting KJ Duff cook. The stud wide out made an insane catch for a TD and added another. The def

item.title: Jason Whitlock says Colts firing Chris Ballard is perfect opportunity to get Carlie Irsay-Gordon ‘off the sidelines’
item.description: Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images Jason Whitlock has opined that the firing of the Indianapolis Colts General Manager Chris Ballard should lead to the departure of Carlie Irsay-Gordon from the sidelines. He also revealed a name that the team should bring in as the Team President, which would bring a lot of excitement among Colts fans. The team has struggled in the last few years, failing to make the playoffs since 2021. Since that season, they have failed to even get into double digits in the win column. This led the team to make the decision to fire Ballard, who was with the franchise for 10 years. A big decision was expected to be made as CEO Irsay-Gordon had already made it clear that she wanted results this season, and with the 2-4 start, it seemed that once again the team was going to end up with a poor record. Her involvement has been heavily discussed by NFL analysts and Jason Whitlock is of the firm opinion that she needs to step off the sidelines. Jason Whitlock believes the Indianapolis Colts should appoint Tom Dungy as the President Tom Dungy is probably one of the most popular names in Indianapolis, as he was the coach who helped the team win their last Super Bowl trophy. Since retiring from coaching, he was with NBC, working as an analyst, but he was fired by the broadcaster in February. This means that the coach is available for the Colts if they need him, but Whitlock’s reasoning behind suggesting his name as the President was for different reasons. “First thing the Colts need to do is hire Tony Dungy as team president. Give their girlboss owner someone to sit with in the press box and explain football to her. Get her off the sidelines. Let everything else flow from that pairing,” Whitlock said. It is not clear if Dungy wants to return to the NFL. At 71, being a Team President is going to be a huge challenge, which is why it is unclear whether Dungy would even take the responsibility or the team would even ask him. Even if he decided against joining the team, Dungy will always be an Indianapolis legend. As far as Irsay-Gordon is concerned, she will definitely continue to be a topic of discussion throughout the NFL season. She had already made a statement with her remarks at the start of the season when she said: “I’ve told Chris and Shane, the sense of urgency has never been higher, and we have to find a way.” During the season, Gordon has been spotted taking down notes and even asking coaches about the decisions that are being made. This is not something traditional CEOs have done, which is why many have raised questions about her methods, but having made the first big decision, it is clear that she is not afraid to make the huge calls for the betterment of the team. item.title: LIV Golf missed a huge opportunity for a unique selling point that would have changed everything
item.description: Photo by Joseph Weiser/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images LIV Golf burst onto the professional golfing scene back in June 2022 with one sole ambition: to topple the PGA Tour. The powers that be at LIV Golf may dispute that statement, but it was obvious for everyone to see that they wanted to end the PGA Tour. They signed huge names from the PGA Tour, including the likes of Bryson DeChambeau, Jon Rahm, Cam Smith, Brooks Koepka, Dustin Johnson and Phil Mickelson. LIV Golf was loud, brash, in-your-face and, quite frankly, everything that the PGA Tour wasn’t. However, while some people warmed to LIV, there was always something missing. The biggest problem they had was the fact that the tournaments were meaningless. Without any history or prestige, tournament wins carried no intrinsic meaning, and golf fans in general struggled to warm to the product. Plenty of mistakes were made along the way, but perhaps their biggest error was failing to grasp the glaring gap in the market regarding the timing of their schedule. LIV Golf missed an opportunity for a unique selling point One of LIV Golf’s major mistakes was believing that staunch PGA Tour fans would be drawn to their product. With that in mind, why didn’t LIV Golf attempt to exist alongside the PGA Tour rather than compete directly with them? They had an obvious opportunity to do exactly that by simply setting up their schedule differently. The current PGA Tour season runs from January to the end of August, and that is set to be condensed down to around seven months from 2028 onwards. Meanwhile, LIV’s season ran from February through to August. The best move they could have made would have been to set up their schedule to run from October through to early July. This would have had two big benefits, one for themselves and one for golf fans in general. LIV Golf would then have had two or three months early on in their season when none of the big PGA Tour events were being played. They could have played their Australian and South African events in November and December, with the eyes of the golfing world tuned in. This would have been great for golf fans because the dead time of the year with no big events would have been filled up with stellar fields on LIV Golf. The LIV Golf hierarchy from the early days will undoubtedly admit that they made plenty of mistakes, and they have proven to be costly with the product almost certainly now finished as a major golf tour. However, failing to take advantage of the huge opportunity they had for a unique selling point by adjusting their schedule was arguably the most costly error of the lot.
